sentences.zh: 良玉少孤，育于叔父。

translations.literal: Liangyu was orphaned young and was raised by his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu lost his parents in childhood and was brought up by his uncle.

sentences.zh: 其貴也，不知其母姓。

translations.literal: When he became eminent, he did not know his mother's surname.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he rose to prominence, he no longer even knew his mother's family name.

sentences.zh: 長身赬面，驍勇，善左右射。

translations.literal: Tall in stature, ruddy-faced, fierce and brave, skilled at shooting to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and ruddy-faced, ferocious in battle, and adept at shooting from either side while mounted.

sentences.zh: 目不知書，多智謀，撫士卒得其歡心，以故戰輒有功。

translations.literal: His eyes did not know books; he had much wisdom and stratagem; he soothed soldiers and won their hearts—therefore in battle he repeatedly had achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Though illiterate, he was shrewd and resourceful; he knew how to win his men over, and for that reason he seldom fought without success.

sentences.zh: 時陝西賊入河南，圖懷慶。

translations.literal: At that time bandits from Shaanxi entered Henan, aiming at Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel forces from Shaanxi poured into Henan and threatened Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 廷議令良玉將昌平兵往剿，大指專辦河南。

translations.literal: The court deliberated and ordered Liangyu to lead the Changping troops to suppress them, with the general intent to focus on Henan alone.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided to send Liangyu at the head of the Changping garrison to suppress them, with the main effort confined to Henan.

sentences.zh: 會賊寇修武、清化者竄入平陽，因檄良玉入山西禦之，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: Meanwhile bandits raiding Xiuwu and Qinghua slipped into Pingyang; an order was therefore sent for Liangyu to enter Shanxi to resist them, and he achieved considerable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile rebels raiding Xiuwu and Qinghua slipped into Pingyang, so Liangyu was ordered into Shanxi to meet them and won a fair number of kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫樊尚璟以良玉駐澤州，扼豫、晉咽侯，可四面為援兵。

translations.literal: Henan governor Fan Shangjing argued that if Liangyu garrisoned Zezhou he would hold the throat of the Henan–Shanxi route and could serve as relief from all four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Henan governor Fan Shangjing urged that Liangyu be posted at Zezhou to hold the strategic throat between Henan and Shanxi, whence he could reinforce operations on every front.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An imperial edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時曹文詔將陝西兵，帝令良玉受尚璟節制，與文詔同心討賊，有急則秦兵東，豫兵西，良玉兵從中橫擊。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Wenzhao commanded the Shaanxi army; the emperor ordered Liangyu to accept Shangjing's command, to work with Wenzhao in heart-and-mind suppression of bandits—with emergency, Qin troops east, Yu troops west, and Liangyu's troops striking horizontally from the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhao then commanded the Shaanxi forces; the emperor placed Liangyu under Shangjing's command and told him to cooperate with Wenzhao—if the rebels pressed hard, Shaanxi troops would strike east, Henan troops west, and Liangyu's men would cut in from the center.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，賊犯隰州，陷陽城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, bandits attacked Xizhou and took Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year, the rebels attacked Xizhou and captured Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 良玉敗之於涉縣之西陂。

translations.literal: Liangyu defeated them at Xipo in She County.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu routed them at Xipo in She County.

sentences.zh: 二月，良玉兵與賊戰武安，大敗。

translations.literal: In the second month, Liangyu's troops fought the bandits at Wu'an and were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month his army met the rebels at Wu'an and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 尚璟罷，乙太常少卿玄默代之。

translations.literal: Shangjing was dismissed, and Vice Minister of Rites Xuan Mo was transferred to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjing was removed from office, and Vice Minister of Rites Xuan Mo was transferred in his place.

sentences.zh: 三月，賊再入河內，良玉自輝縣逐之。

translations.literal: In the third month, bandits again entered Henei; Liangyu pursued them from Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the rebels again entered Henei, and Liangyu pursued them from Huixian.

sentences.zh: 賊奔修武，殺遊擊越效忠，追參將陶希謙，希謙墜馬死。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Xiuwu, killed guerrilla commander Yue Xiaozhong, pursued Assistant Commander Tao Xiqian, and Xiqian fell from his horse and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Xiuwu, killed guerrilla commander Yue Xiaozhong, and chased down Assistant Commander Tao Xiqian, who fell from his horse and was killed.

sentences.zh: 良玉擊之萬善驛，至柳樹口大敗之，擒賊首數人，賊遂西奔。

translations.literal: Liangyu struck them at Wanshan Post, and at Willow Tree Pass greatly defeated them, capturing several bandit chiefs; the bandits then fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu struck them at Wanshan Post and then inflicted a major defeat at Willow Tree Pass, taking several rebel leaders; the rebels then fled west.

sentences.zh: 河南額兵僅七千，數被賊，折亡殆盡。

translations.literal: Henan's quota troops numbered only seven thousand; repeatedly struck by bandits, they were nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's allotted troops numbered only seven thousand; after repeated defeats by the rebels they were nearly annihilated.

sentences.zh: 良玉將昌平兵二千余，數戰，雖有功，勢孤甚。

translations.literal: Liangyu led a little more than two thousand Changping troops; though he fought many times and had achievements, his position was very isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu had a little over two thousand Changping troops; though he fought repeatedly and won some victories, he was dangerously isolated.

sentences.zh: 總兵鄧方立功萊州，乃命將川兵益以石砫土司馬鳳儀兵馳赴良玉，與共角賊。

translations.literal: Regional commander Deng Yan was then achieving merit at Laizhou; he was therefore ordered to lead Sichuan troops, augmented by the native-official troops of Shizhu tusi Ma Fengyi, to hurry to Liangyu and together grapple with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Deng Yan was then winning laurels at Laizhou, so he was ordered to lead Sichuan troops, reinforced by the Shizhu native commander Ma Fengyi's forces, to Liangyu's aid to engage the rebels together.

sentences.zh: 已而鳳儀以孤軍戰沒于侯家莊。

translations.literal: Before long Fengyi, fighting with an isolated army, was killed in action at Houjiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fengyi was killed in action at Houjiazhuang, fighting with an isolated detachment.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊勢已大熾，縱橫三晉、畿輔、河北間。

translations.literal: At this time bandit power was already greatly blazing, ranging across the three Jin provinces, the capital region, and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebels had grown formidable, ranging across Shanxi, the capital region, and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 諸將曹文詔、李卑、艾萬年、湯九州、鄧、良玉等先後與賊戰，勝負略相當。

translations.literal: The generals Cao Wenzhao, Li Bei, Ai Wannian, Tang Jiuzhou, Deng Yan, Liangyu, and others successively fought the bandits; victory and defeat were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Generals such as Cao Wenzhao, Li Bei, Ai Wannian, Tang Jiuzhou, Deng Yan, and Liangyu fought the rebels in turn, with neither side gaining a clear upper hand.

sentences.zh: 良玉、辦河南，屢破之於官村，於沁河，於清化，于萬善。

translations.literal: Liangyu and Yan handled Henan and repeatedly broke them at Guancun, on the Qin River, at Qinghua, and at Wanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu and Deng Yan, operating in Henan, repeatedly defeated them at Guancun, on the Qin River, at Qinghua, and at Wanshan.

sentences.zh: 良玉又扼之武安八德，斬獲尤多。

translations.literal: Liangyu again blocked them at Bade in Wu'an, with especially many kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu also blocked them at Bade in Wu'an and took an especially large toll in kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 會帝命倪寵、王朴為總兵，將京營兵六千赴河南，以中官楊進朝、盧九德監其軍，而別遣中官監良玉等軍。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Ni Chong and Wang Pu as regional commanders, leading six thousand capital-garrison troops to Henan, with eunuchs Yang Jinchao and Lu Jiude supervising their army, while separately dispatching eunuchs to supervise Liangyu's army and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed Ni Chong and Wang Pu regional commanders and sent six thousand capital-garrison troops to Henan under the supervision of eunuchs Yang Jinchao and Lu Jiude, while dispatching other eunuchs to oversee Liangyu and the rest.

sentences.zh: 職方郎中李繼貞曰：「良玉、李卑身經百戰，位反在寵、樸下，恐聞而解體。

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs director Li Jizhen said: "Liangyu and Li Bei have personally undergone a hundred battles, yet their ranks stand below Chong and Pu—fearing that on hearing this the armies will dissolve."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Li Jizhen said, "Liangyu and Li Bei are veterans of a hundred battles, yet they rank below Chong and Pu; I fear the troops will lose heart when they hear of it.

sentences.zh: 」乃令良玉、卑署都督僉事，為援剿總兵官，與寵、樸體相敵。

translations.literal: " He therefore ordered Liangyu and Bei provisionally appointed Vice Commissioners-in-chief, as relief-suppression regional commanders, equal in standing to Chong and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: " Liangyu and Bei were therefore given acting appointments as Vice Commissioners-in-chief and made relief-suppression regional commanders, equal in rank to Chong and Pu.

sentences.zh: 京營兵至，共擊賊，數有功。

translations.literal: When the capital-garrison troops arrived, all together struck the bandits and repeatedly had achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital troops arrived, the combined forces struck the rebels repeatedly with success.

sentences.zh: 良玉敗賊濟源、河內，又敗之永甯青山嶺銀洞溝，又自葉縣追至小武當山，皆斬賊魁甚眾。

translations.literal: Liangyu defeated bandits at Jiyuan and Henei, again defeated them at Yindong Gully on Qingshan Ridge in Yongning, and again from Ye County pursued to Little Wudang Mountain—all with very many bandit chiefs beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu defeated the rebels at Jiyuan and Henei, again at Silver Cave Gully on Qingshan Ridge in Yongning, and pursued them from Ye County to Little Wudang Mountain, beheading a great many rebel leaders each time.

sentences.zh: 然諸將以中官監軍，意弗善也。

translations.literal: Yet the generals, because eunuchs supervised the armies, were not of good mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the generals deeply resented eunuch supervision of their commands.

sentences.zh: 其冬，賊西奔者復折而東。

translations.literal: That winter, those bandits who had fled west turned back east again.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels who had fled west turned back east.

sentences.zh: 良玉、九州扼其前，京營兵尾其後，賊大困，官軍連破之柳泉、猛虎村。

translations.literal: Liangyu and Jiuzhou blocked them in front, capital-garrison troops followed their rear; the bandits were greatly trapped, and the government armies successively broke them at Liuquan and Fierce Tiger Village.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu and Tang Jiuzhou blocked them in front while the capital troops harried their rear; hard pressed, the rebels were beaten in succession at Liuquan and Fierce Tiger Village.

sentences.zh: 賊張妙手、賀雙全等三十六家詭詞乞撫於分巡布政司常道立，因監軍進朝以請。

translations.literal: The bandits Zhang Miaoshou, He Shuangquan, and thirty-six other bands used specious words to beg surrender from the circuit-intendant administrative commissioner Chang Daoli, and through supervising eunuch Jinchao requested it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miaoshou, He Shuangquan, and thirty-six other rebel bands petitioned circuit intendant Chang Daoli with feigned offers of surrender, and asked through supervising eunuch Jinchao for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 諸將俟朝命，不出戰。

translations.literal: The generals awaited court orders and did not go out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The generals held their lines awaiting court orders and did not engage.

sentences.zh: 會天寒河冰合，賊遂從澠池徑渡，巡撫默率良玉、九州、卑、兵待之境上。

translations.literal: It happened that the weather was cold and the river ice joined; the bandits then crossed directly from Mianchi, and Governor Mo led Liangyu, Jiuzhou, Bei, and Yan's troops to wait for them on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Then the weather turned cold, the rivers froze, and the rebels crossed directly from Mianchi; Governor Xuan Mo led Liangyu, Jiuzhou, Bei, and Deng Yan's troops to meet them on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 賊乃竄盧氏山中，由此自鄖、襄入川中，折而掠秦隴，復出沒川中、湖北，以犯河南，中原益大殘破，而三晉、畿輔獨不受賊禍者十年。

translations.literal: The bandits then fled into the Lu Clan mountains, from there from Yun and Xiang entered Sichuan, turned to plunder Qin and Long, again emerged and vanished in Sichuan and Hubei to invade Henan; the Central Plain grew ever more greatly ravaged, while the three Jin provinces and the capital region alone did not suffer bandit calamity for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped into the Lu Clan mountains, entered Sichuan by way of Yun and Xiang, turned to raid Qin and Long, and then ranged through Sichuan and Hubei before striking Henan again; the Central Plain was laid waste, while Shanxi and the capital region alone escaped rebel devastation for a decade.

sentences.zh: 賊既渡河去，良玉與諸將分地守。

translations.literal: After the bandits had crossed the river and gone, Liangyu and the generals divided territory to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels had crossed the river and departed, Liangyu and the other generals divided the territory among themselves for defense.

sentences.zh: 陳奇瑜、盧象升方角賊秦、楚，七年春夏間，中州幸無事。

translations.literal: Chen Qiyu and Lu Xiangsheng were then grappling with bandits in Qin and Chu; in spring and summer of the seventh year the Central Plain fortunately had no incidents.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiyu and Lu Xiangsheng were then fighting the rebels in Shaanxi and Huguang; through the spring and summer of the seventh year the Central Plain was spared trouble.

sentences.zh: 既而奇瑜失李自成於車箱，廷議合晉、豫、楚、蜀兵四面剿之。

translations.literal: Before long Qiyu lost Li Zicheng at Chexiang; the court deliberated to combine Jin, Yu, Chu, and Shu troops to suppress them on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qiyu let Li Zicheng slip away at Chexiang, and the court resolved to combine forces from Shanxi, Henan, Huguang, and Sichuan for a four-front suppression.

sentences.zh: 賊乃分軍三：一向慶陽，一趨鄖陽，而一出關趨河南。

translations.literal: The bandits then divided their army into three: one toward Qingyang, one hurrying to Yunyang, and one out of the pass hurrying to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then split into three columns: one toward Qingyang, one toward Yunyang, and one through the pass into Henan.

sentences.zh: 趨河南者又分為三，郡邑所在告急。

translations.literal: Those hurrying to Henan again divided into three; wherever prefectures and counties were, urgent reports came.
translations.idiomatic: The column bound for Henan split again into three, and distress calls poured in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 良玉扼新安、澠池，他將陳治邦駐汝州，陳永福扼南陽，皆坐甲自保而已，不能大創賊也。

translations.literal: Liangyu blocked Xin'an and Mianchi; other generals Chen Zhibang garrisoned Ruzhou, Chen Yongfu blocked Nanyang—all merely sat with armor to protect themselves and could not greatly wound the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu held Xin'an and Mianchi; Chen Zhibang garrisoned Ruzhou and Chen Yongfu Nanyang—they merely kept their troops in camp for self-protection and could not inflict a decisive blow on the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊每營數萬，兵番進，皆因糧宿飽；

translations.literal: The bandits each camped in tens of thousands; troops advanced in rotation, all because of grain lodging and being full;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels camped in tens of thousands at a time, advancing in relays and living off the land;

sentences.zh: 我兵寡備多，饋餉不繼。

translations.literal: our troops were few with many garrisons, and provisions did not continue.
translations.idiomatic: our troops were few but our garrisons many, and supplies could not keep up.

sentences.zh: 賊介馬馳，一日夜數百里；

translations.literal: The bandits, with armored horses galloping, covered several hundred li in one day and night;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rode armored horses and covered hundreds of li in a day and night;

sentences.zh: 我步兵多，騎少，行數十里輒疲乏，以故多畏賊。

translations.literal: our infantry was many, cavalry few; after going several tens of li they were soon exhausted—therefore many feared the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: our forces were mostly infantry with little cavalry, and men tired after only a few dozen li—so government troops widely feared the rebels.

sentences.zh: 而良玉在懷慶時，與督撫議不合，因是生心，緩追養寇，多收降者以自重。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Liangyu was at Huaiqing, he did not agree with the governor-general and governors; because of this he harbored resentment, pursued slowly and nourished bandits, and received many who surrendered to increase his own weight.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile, while posted at Huaiqing, Liangyu had fallen out with his superiors; he therefore grew disaffected, pursued half-heartedly and let the rebels grow stronger, and took in many surrendering bands to swell his own power.

sentences.zh: 督撫檄調，不時應命，稍稍露跋扈端矣。

translations.literal: When governor-generals and governors issued orders, he did not respond to commands in timely fashion, and little by little showed signs of arrogance and defiance.
translations.idiomatic: He no longer answered summons promptly, and began to show signs of arrogance and defiance.

sentences.zh: 十二月遇賊於磁山，大戰數十，追奔百餘里。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he encountered bandits at Cishan, fought great battles several tens of times, and pursued the fleeing enemy more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he met the rebels at Cishan, fought dozens of engagements, and pursued them for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，河南賊破潁州，毀鳳陽皇陵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year, Henan bandits took Yingzhou and destroyed the imperial tombs at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year Henan rebels captured Yingzhou and desecrated the imperial tombs at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 其陷鹿邑、柘城、寧陵、通許者，良玉在許州不能救。

translations.literal: As for those who took Luyi, Zhecheng, Ningling, and Tongxu, Liangyu was at Xuzhou and could not rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When Luyi, Zhecheng, Ningling, and Tongxu fell, Liangyu was at Xuzhou and could not relieve them.

sentences.zh: 四月，督師洪承疇在汝州，令諸將分地遮賊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, supreme commander Hong Chengchou was at Ruzhou and ordered the generals to divide territory to intercept bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month supreme commander Hong Chengchou was at Ruzhou and ordered the generals to divide the territory and block the rebels.

sentences.zh: 尤世威守雒南，陳永福控盧氏、永甯，鄧、尤翟文、張應昌、許成名遏湖廣。

translations.literal: You Shiwei guarded Luonan; Chen Yongfu controlled Lu Clan and Yongning; Deng Yan, You Zhaiwen, Zhang Yingchang, and Xu Chengming blocked Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: You Shiwei held Luonan; Chen Yongfu controlled Lu Clan and Yongning; Deng Yan, You Zhaiwen, Zhang Yingchang, and Xu Chengming blocked the route into Huguang.

sentences.zh: 以吳村、瓦屋乃內鄉、淅川要地，令良玉與湯九州以五千人扼之。

translations.literal: Because Wucun and Wawu were strategic places of Neixiang and Xichuan, he ordered Liangyu and Tang Jiuzhou with five thousand men to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wucun and Wawu were vital points on the Neixiang–Xichuan route, he ordered Liangyu and Tang Jiuzhou to hold them with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鄧圯以兵嘩死，而曹文詔討陝賊，敗沒于真寧。

translations.literal: Before long Deng Yan died in a mutiny, while Cao Wenzhao, suppressing Shaanxi bandits, was defeated and killed at Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Deng Yan died in a mutiny, and Cao Wenzhao, campaigning against Shaanxi rebels, was defeated and killed at Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 賊益張，遂超盧氏，奔永寧。

translations.literal: The bandits grew ever more powerful and then passed over Lu Clan, fleeing to Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew bolder still, crossed Lu Clan territory, and fled toward Yongning.

sentences.zh: 巡撫默被逮未去，檄良玉自內鄉與陳治邦、馬良文等援盧氏。

translations.literal: Governor Mo, though arrested, had not yet departed; he ordered Liangyu from Neixiang with Chen Zhibang, Ma Liangwen, and others to relieve Lu Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xuan Mo, though under arrest and not yet removed, ordered Liangyu from Neixiang, together with Chen Zhibang, Ma Liangwen, and others, to relieve Lu Clan.

sentences.zh: 八月敗賊于鄢陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he defeated bandits at Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he defeated the rebels at Yanling.

sentences.zh: 九月躡賊於郟之神垕山。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he tracked bandits to Spirit Mound Mountain in Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he pursued the rebels to Spirit Mound Mountain in Jia.

sentences.zh: 賊連營數十里，番休更戰，以疲我兵，良玉收其軍而止。

translations.literal: The bandits linked camps for several tens of li, rested in rotation and fought in alternation to weary our troops; Liangyu withdrew his army and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels strung their camps along several tens of li, fighting in relays to wear down government troops; Liangyu drew off his army and broke off.

sentences.zh: 賊再攻密，良玉自郟援之，乃去。

translations.literal: The bandits again attacked Mi; Liangyu from Jia relieved it, and they then departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked Mi again, Liangyu marched from Jia to its relief and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十月，良玉抵靈寶，合遼東總兵祖寬兵剪賊於澗口、焦村。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Liangyu reached Lingbao, joined Liaodong regional commander Zu Kuan's troops, and cut down bandits at Jian Pass and Jiaocun.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Liangyu reached Lingbao, joined Liaodong commander Zu Kuan, and cut up the rebels at Jian Pass and Jiaocun.

sentences.zh: 焦村，硃陽關地也。

translations.literal: Jiaocun is territory of Zhuyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaocun lies in the territory of Zhuyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 十一月，李自成出硃陽關，張獻忠久據靈寶，闖王高迎祥亦與合。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Li Zicheng came out of Zhuyang Pass; Zhang Xianzhong had long held Lingbao, and Surge King Gao Yingxiang also joined with them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Li Zicheng came out through Zhuyang Pass; Zhang Xianzhong had long held Lingbao, and Surge King Gao Yingxiang joined them as well.

sentences.zh: 良玉、寬禦之靈寶，不能支，陝州陷。

translations.literal: Liangyu and Kuan defended at Lingbao but could not hold; Shanzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu and Zu Kuan defended Lingbao but could not hold, and Shanzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 賊東下攻洛陽，良玉、寬從巡撫陳必謙救洛陽，賊乃去。

translations.literal: The bandits went east to attack Luoyang; Liangyu and Kuan followed Governor Chen Biqian to relieve Luoyang, and the bandits then departed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels marched east against Luoyang; Liangyu and Zu Kuan followed Governor Chen Biqian to its relief, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 迎祥、自成走偃師、鞏。

translations.literal: Yingxiang and Zicheng fled to Yanshi and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yingxiang and Li Zicheng fled toward Yanshi and Gong.

sentences.zh: 獻忠走嵩、汝。

translations.literal: Xianzhong fled to Song and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong fled toward Song and Ru.

sentences.zh: 良玉出雒追迎祥、自成。

translations.literal: Liangyu went out from Luo to pursue Yingxiang and Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu marched out from Luoyang to pursue Gao Yingxiang and Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 寬分擊獻忠救汝。

translations.literal: Kuan separately struck Xianzhong to relieve Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Kuan struck at Zhang Xianzhong to relieve Ru prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會總理盧象升至自湖廣，與寬大敗賊汝西，令裨將破賊于宜陽黃澗口。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Lu Xiangsheng arrived from Huguang, and with Kuan greatly defeated bandits west of Ru, ordering a subordinate general to break bandits at Huangjian Pass in Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Lu Xiangsheng arrived from Huguang; with Zu Kuan he inflicted a major defeat west of Ru, and a subordinate routed the rebels at Huangjian Pass in Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，賊敗于登封郜城鎮，走石陽關，與伊、嵩之賊合。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year, bandits were defeated at Gaocheng Town in Dengfeng, fled to Shiyang Pass, and joined with bandits of Yi and Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year the rebels were beaten at Gaocheng in Dengfeng, fled to Shiyang Pass, and joined forces with the bands in the Yi and Song ranges.

sentences.zh: 故總兵九州由嵩縣深入，與良玉夾剿。

translations.literal: Former regional commander Jiuzhou from Song County advanced deeply, and with Liangyu pincered in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Former commander Tang Jiuzhou advanced deep from Song County to attack them in concert with Liangyu.

sentences.zh: 良玉中道遁歸，九州乘勝窮追四十里，無援敗歿，良玉反以捷聞。

translations.literal: Liangyu midway fled back; Jiuzhou, riding victory, pursued to the limit forty li, without relief was defeated and killed; Liangyu nevertheless reported a victory.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu slipped away midway; Jiuzhou pressed the pursuit for forty li without support, was defeated and killed, while Liangyu reported a victory.

sentences.zh: 五月，象升遣祖寬、李重鎮隨陝西總督洪承疇西行。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Xiangsheng dispatched Zu Kuan and Li Chongzhen to follow Shaanxi governor-general Hong Chengchou west.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Lu Xiangsheng sent Zu Kuan and Li Chongzhen west with Shaanxi governor-general Hong Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 良玉軍最強，又率中州人，故獨久留之。

translations.literal: Liangyu's army was strongest, and moreover he led Central Plain men—therefore alone he was long retained.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu's army was the strongest and composed largely of men from the Central Plain, so he alone was kept in the region.

sentences.zh: 而以其驕亢難用，用孔道興代其偏將趙柱駐靈寶，防雒西；

translations.literal: Yet because he was proud and overbearing and hard to employ, Kong Daoxing was used to replace his deputy general Zhao Zhu garrisoning Lingbao to defend west of Luo;
translations.idiomatic: But because he was proud and unmanageable, Kong Daoxing replaced his deputy Zhao Zhu at Lingbao to guard the western approaches to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 良玉與羅岱駐宜、永，防雒東。

translations.literal: Liangyu with Luo Dai garrisoned Yi and Yong to defend east of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu and Luo Dai were posted at Yiyang and Yongning to guard the eastern approaches.

sentences.zh: 七月，良玉兵抵開封，由登封之唐莊深入擊賊，自辰鏖至申，賊不支西走。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Liangyu's troops reached Kaifeng, from Tangzhuang in Dengfeng advanced deeply to strike bandits, from the chen hour fought fiercely to the shen hour; the bandits could not hold and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Liangyu reached Kaifeng, advanced from Tangzhuang in Dengfeng, and fought from morning until late afternoon; the rebels gave way and fled west.

sentences.zh: 陳永福方敗賊于唐河，賊至田家營，良玉渡河擊之，斬獲頗眾。

translations.literal: Chen Yongfu had just defeated bandits at Tang River; when bandits reached Tianjia Camp, Liangyu crossed the river to strike them, with quite many kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yongfu had just defeated the rebels on the Tang River; when they reached Tianjia Camp, Liangyu crossed the river and struck them, taking a large toll in kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 九月，巡撫楊繩武劾良玉避賊，責令戴罪自贖。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Governor Yang Shengwu impeached Liangyu for avoiding bandits and ordered him to redeem guilt while bearing punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Governor Yang Shengwu impeached Liangyu for shirking combat and ordered him to redeem himself while under demerit.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，賊老回回合曹操、闖塌天諸部沿流東下，安慶告警，詔良玉從中州救之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, bandit Old Huihe united Cao Cao, Collapse-the-Sky, and other bands along the river eastward; Anqing sounded alarm, and an edict ordered Liangyu from the Central Plain to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year Old Huihe united the bands of Cao Cao and Collapse-the-Sky and marched downriver east; when Anqing was threatened, Liangyu was ordered from the Central Plain to its relief.

sentences.zh: 良玉道剿殺南陽土寇楊四、侯馭民、郭三海，急抵六安，與賊遇。

translations.literal: Liangyu on the way suppressed and killed Nanyang local bandits Yang Si, Hou Yumin, and Guo Sanhai, hurried to Lu'an, and encountered bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On the march Liangyu wiped out the Nanyang bandits Yang Si, Hou Yumin, and Guo Sanhai, hurried to Lu'an, and met the rebels.

sentences.zh: 部將岱、道興乘勝連戰，大破賊。

translations.literal: Deputy generals Dai and Daoxing, riding victory, fought in succession and greatly broke the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His deputies Luo Dai and Kong Daoxing pressed the advantage in repeated engagements and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊走霍、潛山。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Huo and Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled toward Huo prefecture and Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 會馬爌、劉良佐亦屢敗賊於桐城、廬州、六安，賊在滁、和者亦西遁，江北警少息。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Ma Xiang and Liu Liangzuo also repeatedly defeated bandits at Tongcheng, Luzhou, and Lu'an; those bandits at Chuzhou and He also fled west, and alarms on the north bank of the Yangtze slightly subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Ma Xiang and Liu Liangzuo also won repeated victories at Tongcheng, Luzhou, and Lu'an; the rebels in Chuzhou and He fled west as well, and the alarm on the north bank of the Yangtze eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 應天巡撫張國維三檄良玉入山搜剿，不應，放兵掠婦女。

translations.literal: Yingtian governor Zhang Guowei thrice ordered Liangyu into the mountains to search and suppress; he did not respond, and let his troops loose to plunder women.
translations.idiomatic: Yingtian governor Zhang Guowei three times ordered Liangyu into the mountains to hunt the rebels down; he refused, and let his men roam freely looting women.

sentences.zh: 屯舒城月余，河南監軍太監力促之，始北去，賊已飽掠入山矣。

translations.literal: He encamped at Shucheng more than a month; the Henan supervising eunuch strongly urged him, and only then he went north—the bandits had already sated themselves with plunder and entered the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at Shucheng for more than a month until the Henan supervising eunuch pressed him hard; only then did he march north, by which time the rebels had already sacked their fill and vanished into the hills.

sentences.zh: 已，淅川陷，良玉擁兵不救。

translations.literal: Before long Xichuan fell; Liangyu held troops and did not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xichuan fell, and Liangyu, though he had troops in hand, did not go to its relief.

sentences.zh: 以六安破賊功，詔落職戴罪，尋復之。

translations.literal: Because of the achievement of breaking bandits at Lu'an, an edict demoted his office while bearing guilt, and soon restored it.
translations.idiomatic: For his victory at Lu'an he was demoted but allowed to redeem himself, and soon restored to rank.

sentences.zh: 賊東下襲六合，攻天長，分掠瓜洲、儀真，破盱眙。

translations.literal: The bandits went east to raid Liuhe, attacked Tianchang, separately plundered Guazhou and Yizhen, and took Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels marched east, raided Liuhe, attacked Tianchang, plundered Guazhou and Yizhen, and captured Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 良玉堅不肯救，令中州士大夫合疏留己。

translations.literal: Liangyu firmly refused to rescue, and ordered Central Plain scholar-officials jointly to memorialize to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu flatly refused to intervene and had Central Plain officials submit a joint memorial asking that he be kept in post.

sentences.zh: 帝知出良玉意，不能奪也。

translations.literal: The emperor knew it came from Liangyu's intent, and could not wrest it away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew this was Liangyu's doing and could not overrule him.

sentences.zh: 十月，總理熊文燦至安慶，部檄以良玉軍隸焉，良玉輕文燦不為用。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan arrived at Anqing; a ministry dispatch placed Liangyu's army under him, but Liangyu looked down on Wencan and would not serve.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Grand Coordinator Xiong Wencan reached Anqing, and orders came placing Liangyu's army under his command; Liangyu despised Wencan and refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，良玉與總兵陳洪范大破賊於鄖西。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, Liangyu together with regional commander Chen Hongfan greatly defeated the bandits at Yuxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year eleven Liangyu and regional commander Chen Hongfan inflicted a crushing defeat on the rebels at Yuxi.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠假官旗號襲南陽，屯于南關。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong, using false official banners and insignia, raided Nanyang and encamped at the southern gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong attacked Nanyang under false imperial colors and camped outside the southern gate.

sentences.zh: 良玉適至，疑而急召之，獻忠逸去。

translations.literal: Liangyu happened to arrive, grew suspicious, and urgently summoned them; Xianzhong slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu happened to arrive, grew suspicious, and sent an urgent summons; Xianzhong fled before he could be seized.

sentences.zh: 追及，發兩矢，中其肩，復揮刀擊之，面流血。

translations.literal: Pursuit caught up; he loosed two arrows, striking his shoulder, then swung a blade and struck him, and blood flowed from his face.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers caught up; Liangyu shot twice and hit Xianzhong in the shoulder, then hacked at him with a blade until his face ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 其部下救以免，遂逃之穀城。

translations.literal: His subordinates rescued him so he escaped harm, and he then fled to Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His men pulled him free, and he escaped to Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，請降，良玉知其偽，力請擊之，文燦不許。

translations.literal: Before long he asked to surrender; Liangyu knew it was feigned and urgently requested to attack him, but Wencan would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xianzhong offered to surrender; Liangyu saw through the ruse and pressed hard for an attack, but Wencan refused.

sentences.zh: 九月，文燦剿鄖、襄諸賊，良玉與洪范及副將龍在田擊破之雙溝營，斬首二千餘級。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wencan suppressed the bandits of Yun and Xiang; Liangyu, Hongfan, and vice commander Long Zaitian broke them at Shuanggou camp and beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, as Wencan campaigned against the Yun and Xiang rebels, Liangyu, Hongfan, and vice commander Long Zaitian routed them at Shuanggou camp and took more than two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 十二月，河南巡撫常道立調良玉於陝州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Henan governor Chang Daoli transferred Liangyu to Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Henan governor Chang Daoli ordered Liangyu to Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊乘盧氏虛，遁入內、淅。

translations.literal: The bandits, seizing Lushi's emptiness, slipped into Neixiang and Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels exploited the gap at Lushi and slipped into Neixiang and Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 是月，許州兵變，良玉家在許，殲焉。

translations.literal: That month soldiers mutinied at Xuzhou; Liangyu's family was at Xu and was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: That same month troops mutinied at Xuzhou, where Liangyu's family lived, and they were slaughtered to the last.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，良玉率降將劉國能入援京師，詔還討河南賊。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year Liangyu led the surrendered general Liu Guoneng to relieve the capital; an edict ordered him back to campaign against Henan bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year twelve Liangyu marched the surrendered general Liu Guoneng to the capital's relief, then was ordered back to fight the Henan rebels.

sentences.zh: 兵過灞頭、吳橋，大掠，太監盧九德疏聞，詔令戴罪。

translations.literal: As the army passed Batou and Wuqiao it plundered heavily; eunuch Lu Jiude memorialized the court, and an edict ordered him to bear guilt.
translations.idiomatic: On the march through Batou and Wuqiao his men looted on a large scale; eunuch Lu Jiude reported it, and the throne ordered Liangyu to serve under demotion.

sentences.zh: 已而破賊馬進忠於鎮平關。

translations.literal: Before long he defeated the bandit Ma Jinzhong at Zhenping Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He soon afterward defeated the rebel Ma Jinzhong at Zhenping Pass.

sentences.zh: 進忠降。

translations.literal: Jinzhong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong submitted.

sentences.zh: 又與國能再破賊李萬慶于張家林、七里河，萬慶亦降。

translations.literal: Again with Guoneng he twice defeated the bandit Li Wanqing at Zhangjialin and Qilihe, and Wanqing also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Guoneng he again defeated Li Wanqing at Zhangjialin and Qilihe, and Wanqing surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 七月，獻忠叛去，良玉與羅岱追之，使岱為前鋒，己隨其後。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Xianzhong rebelled and left; Liangyu and Luo Dai pursued him, making Dai the vanguard while he himself followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xianzhong broke away again; Liangyu and Luo Dai pursued, with Dai in the van and Liangyu behind.

sentences.zh: 逾房縣八十里，至羅猴山，軍乏食。

translations.literal: They crossed eighty li beyond Fang County to Luohou Mountain, and the army lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed eighty li past Fang County to Luohou Mountain, where the army ran out of provisions.

sentences.zh: 伏起，岱馬掛於藤，抽刀斷之，蹶而復進，棄馬登山，賊圍急，矢盡被獲。

translations.literal: An ambush rose; Dai's horse caught on vines, he drew a blade and severed them, stumbled yet advanced again, abandoned the horse and climbed the mountain; the bandits pressed the encirclement hard, his arrows were spent, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Ambushers sprang up; Dai's horse snagged in creepers, and he cut himself free, stumbled on, then abandoned the mount and climbed the slope; the rebels closed in, his arrows ran out, and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 良玉大敗奔還，軍符印信盡失，棄軍資千萬余，士卒死者萬人。

translations.literal: Liangyu was greatly defeated and fled back; military tallies and seals were all lost, more than ten million in army stores abandoned, and ten thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu suffered a crushing defeat and fled; he lost his tallies and seals, abandoned supplies worth more than ten million, and left ten thousand dead on the field.

sentences.zh: 事聞，以輕進貶三秩。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, for rash advance he was demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court he was stripped of three ranks for reckless advance.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，督師楊嗣昌薦良玉雖敗，有大將才，兵亦可用，遂拜平賊將軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year, Grand Secretary Yang Sichang recommended that although Liangyu had been defeated, he had great general's talent and his troops were still usable; he was then appointed General Who Pacifies Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year thirteen Grand Secretary Yang Sichang argued that despite his defeat Liangyu still had the makings of a great commander and his army remained serviceable, and he was made General Who Pacifies Bandits.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊分為三：西則張獻忠，踞楚、蜀郊；

translations.literal: At that time the bandits divided into three: in the west was Zhang Xianzhong, holding the borders of Chu and Shu;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebels had split into three groups: in the west Zhang Xianzhong held the Chu and Shu frontier;

sentences.zh: 東則革裏眼、左金王等四營，豕突隨、應、麻、黃；

translations.literal: in the east were Ge Liyan, Zuo Jinwang, and four other camps, charging like swine through Suizhou, Yingzhou, Macheng, and Huangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: in the east Ge Liyan, Zuo Jinwang, and four camps rampaged through Suizhou, Yingzhou, Macheng, and Huangzhou;

sentences.zh: 南則曹操、過天星等十營，伏漳、房、興、遠間。

translations.literal: in the south were Cao Cao, Guo Tianxing, and ten other camps, lying in ambush between Zhang, Fang, Xingshan, and Yuan'an.
translations.idiomatic: in the south Cao Cao, Guo Tianxing, and ten camps lurked among Zhang, Fang, Xingshan, and Yuan'an.

sentences.zh: 閏正月，良玉合諸軍擊賊于枸坪關，獻忠敗走，良玉乃請從漢陽、西鄉入蜀追之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month Liangyu united the armies and struck the bandits at Gouping Pass; Xianzhong was defeated and fled, and Liangyu then requested to enter Shu by way of Hanyang and Xixiang in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month Liangyu combined the armies and beat the rebels at Gouping Pass; Xianzhong fled, and Liangyu asked to pursue into Sichuan through Hanyang and Xixiang.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌謀以陝西總督鄭崇儉率賀人龍、李國奇從西鄉入蜀，而令良玉駐兵興平，別遣偏將追剿，良玉不從。

translations.literal: Sichang planned for Shaanxi governor Zheng Chongjian to lead He Renlong and Li Guoqi into Shu from Xixiang, while ordering Liangyu to station troops at Xingping and separately dispatch a partial general to pursue and suppress; Liangyu would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang intended that Shaanxi governor Zheng Chongjian lead He Renlong and Li Guoqi into Sichuan from Xixiang while Liangyu held at Xingping and a subordinate general carried on the pursuit; Liangyu refused.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌檄良玉曰：「賊勢似不能入川，仍當走死秦界耳。

translations.literal: Sichang dispatched a message to Liangyu, saying: [The rebels' force seems unable to enter Sichuan; they should still flee to perish on the Qin frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang wrote to Liangyu: "The rebels likely cannot push into Sichuan and will instead flee west to die on the Shaanxi border.

sentences.zh: 將軍從漢陽、西鄉入川，萬一賊從舊路疾趨平利，仍入竹、房，將何以禦？

translations.literal: If the general enters Sichuan by way of Hanyang and Xixiang, should the bandits by any chance hurry along the old road toward Pingli and again enter Zhu and Fang, how will you defend?
translations.idiomatic: If you march into Sichuan through Hanyang and Xixiang, and they double back swiftly toward Pingli and re-enter Zhushan and Fangxian, how will you stop them?

sentences.zh: 不則走寧昌，入歸、巫，與曹操合，我以大將尾追，促賊反楚，非算也。

translations.literal: Otherwise they will flee to Ningchang, enter Gui and Wu, join Cao Cao—if I, with a great general, follow at the rear and drive the bandits back into Chu, that is not a sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: Or they may run to Ningchang, slip into Guizhou and Wushan, and unite with Cao Cao; hounding them back into Huguang with our main forces at their heels would be poor strategy."

sentences.zh: 」良玉報曰：「蜀地肥衍，賊渡險任其奔軼，後難制。

translations.literal: ] Liangyu replied: [Sichuan's land is rich and extensive; once bandits cross difficult ground and are let run free, they will later be hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu answered: "Sichuan is rich and broad. If we let them past the defiles to run where they will, they will be hard to control afterward.

sentences.zh: 且賊入川則有糧可因，回鄖則無地可掠，其不復竄楚境明矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, if bandits enter Sichuan they will have grain to rely on; if they return to Yun there will be no land to plunder—their not again fleeing into Chu territory is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside Sichuan they can live off its grain; back in Yun there is nothing left to loot, so they plainly will not bolt back into Huguang.

sentences.zh: 夫兵合則強，分則弱。

translations.literal: Now troops united are strong, divided weak.
translations.idiomatic: Concentrated forces are strong; scattered ones are weak.

sentences.zh: 今已留劉國能、李萬慶守鄖，若再分三千人入蜀，即駐興平，兵力已薄，賊來能遏之耶？

translations.literal: Now Liu Guoneng and Li Wanqing have already been left to guard Yun; if another three thousand men are sent into Shu while one merely stations at Xingping, military strength is already thin—when bandits come, can they be checked?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guoneng and Li Wanqing already hold Yun; if we peel off another three thousand into Sichuan and you merely camp at Xingping, our strength is too thin—how will we stop them when they come?

sentences.zh: 今當出其不意疾攻之，一大創自然瓦解，縱折回房、竹間，人跡斷絕，彼從何得食？

translations.literal: Now one ought to strike them unexpectedly in a swift attack; one great wound and they will naturally disintegrate—even if they turn back between Fang and Zhu, where human traces are cut off, from where will they obtain food?
translations.idiomatic: We should hit them now, before they expect it; one hard blow will break them. Even if they loop back through Fang and Zhu, those hills are deserted—where would they find food?

sentences.zh: 況鄖兵扼之于前，秦撫在紫、興扼之於右，勢必不得逞。

translations.literal: Moreover Yun troops choke them in front, and the Shaanxi governor at Zi and Xing chokes them on the right—they surely cannot prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, our men at Yun will block them ahead and the Shaanxi governor at Ziyang and Xing will close the right— they cannot break through.

sentences.zh: 若甯昌、歸、巫險且遠，曹操、獻忠不相下。

translations.literal: As for Ningchang, Gui, and Wu, they are perilous and far; Cao Cao and Xianzhong do not yield to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ningchang, Guizhou, and Wushan are rugged and remote, and Cao Cao and Xianzhong will not bow to each other.

sentences.zh: 倘窮而歸曹，必內相吞，其亡立見。

translations.literal: If, in desperation, they join Cao, they will surely devour one another within, and their destruction will be immediately seen.
translations.idiomatic: If they throw in with Cao in desperation, they will tear each other apart and perish at once."

sentences.zh: 」良玉已於二月朔涉蜀界之漁溪渡矣。

translations.literal: ] Already on the first of the second month Liangyu had crossed into Shu border at Yuxi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: By then, on the first day of the second month, Liangyu had already crossed into Sichuan at Yuxi Ford.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌度力不能制，而其計良是，遂從之。

translations.literal: Sichang gauged that his power could not control him, yet his plan was truly sound, and so followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang saw he could not compel Liangyu, but judged his plan sound and went along.

sentences.zh: 時獻忠營太平縣大竹河，良玉駐漁溪渡。

translations.literal: At that time Xianzhong was encamped at Dazhu River in Taiping County; Liangyu was stationed at Yuxi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong was then camped on the Dazhu River in Taiping County while Liangyu held Yuxi Ford.

sentences.zh: 未幾，總督崇儉引其兵來會。

translations.literal: Before long Governor Chongjian led his troops to join.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Governor Zheng Chongjian arrived with his troops.

sentences.zh: 賊移軍九滾坪，見瑪瑙山峻險，將據之。

translations.literal: The bandits shifted army to Jiugunping, saw Agate Mountain steep and perilous, and were about to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels moved to Jiugunping and, seeing how steep Agate Mountain was, prepared to hold it.

sentences.zh: 良玉始抵山下，賊已踞山顛，乘高鼓噪。

translations.literal: Liangyu had only just reached the foot of the mountain when the bandits already held the summit, taking the height and beating drums and shouting.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu had barely reached the foot of the slope when the rebels already held the crest, drumming and shouting from above.

sentences.zh: 良玉下馬周覽者久之，曰：「吾知所以破賊矣。

translations.literal: Liangyu dismounted and walked about viewing for a long time, then said: [I know how to break the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu dismounted and studied the ground at length, then said, "I know how to beat them.

sentences.zh: 」分所進道為三，己當其二，秦兵當其一。

translations.literal: ] He divided the advancing routes into three—himself taking two parts, Qin troops taking one.
translations.idiomatic: He split the assault routes into three: he would take two, the Shaanxi troops one.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「聞鼓聲而上。

translations.literal: The order was: [On hearing the drums, advance uphill.
translations.idiomatic: His order ran: "When you hear the drums, go up.

sentences.zh: 」兩軍夾擊，賊陣堅不可動。

translations.literal: ] The two armies struck from both sides; the bandit formation was solid and would not move.
translations.idiomatic: " The two wings closed in, but the rebel line held firm.

sentences.zh: 鏖戰久之，賊大潰，墜崖澗者無算。

translations.literal: After fierce fighting for a long time the bandits were greatly routed; those who fell from cliffs and ravines were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: After a long, bloody fight the rebels broke completely; countless men plunged off the cliffs.

sentences.zh: 追奔四十里，良玉兵斬掃地王曹威、白馬鄧天王等渠魁十六人。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout forty li, Liangyu's troops beheaded sixteen chieftains including Caodi Wang Cao Wei and White Horse Deng Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran forty li, and Liangyu's men killed sixteen rebel leaders, among them Cao Wei the Earth-Scanning King and Deng Yan the White Horse Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 獻忠妻妾亦被擒，遁入興山、歸州之山中，尋自鹽井竄興、歸界上。

translations.literal: Xianzhong's wives and concubines were also captured; he fled into the mountains of Xingshan and Guizhou, and soon from Yanjing slipped along the Xing and Gui border.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong's wives and concubines were taken as well; he vanished into the hills of Xingshan and Guizhou, then slipped from Yanjing back onto the Xing–Gui frontier.

sentences.zh: 是役也，良玉功第一。

translations.literal: In this campaign Liangyu's merit was first.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle Liangyu's achievement ranked first.

sentences.zh: 事聞，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四月，良玉進屯興安、平利諸山，連營百里。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Liangyu advanced and encamped on the mountains of Xing'an and Pingli, camps stretching a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Liangyu pushed into the Xing'an and Pingli ranges and strung camps along a hundred li of ground.

sentences.zh: 諸軍憚山險，圍而不攻。

translations.literal: The various armies feared the mountains' peril and besieged without attacking.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies feared the steep terrain and merely surrounded the rebels without attacking.

sentences.zh: 久之，獻忠自興、房走白羊山而西，與羅汝才合。

translations.literal: After a long while Xianzhong went from Xing and Fang by Baiyang Mountain westward and joined Luo Rucai.
translations.idiomatic: In time Xianzhong broke out through Xing and Fang, crossed Baiyang Mountain westward, and joined Luo Rucai.

sentences.zh: 七月，良玉乘勝擊過天星，降之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Liangyu, riding victory, struck Guo Tianxing and received his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Liangyu pressed his advantage, defeated Guo Tianxing, and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 過天星者，名惠登相，既降，遂始終為良玉部將。

translations.literal: Guo Tianxing's name was Hui Dengxiang; once he had surrendered, he thereafter always served as Liangyu's subordinate general.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tianxing was the rebel name of Hui Dengxiang; after he submitted he remained one of Liangyu's officers to the end.

sentences.zh: 初，良玉受平賊將軍印，浸驕，不肯受督師約束。

translations.literal: At first, when Liangyu received the seal of General Who Pacifies Bandits, he gradually grew arrogant and would not accept the Grand Secretary's constraints.
translations.idiomatic: Once he received the seal of General Who Pacifies Bandits, Liangyu grew steadily more arrogant and refused to obey the Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 而賀人龍屢破賊有功，嗣昌私許以人龍代良玉。

translations.literal: Meanwhile He Renlong had repeatedly broken bandits with merit; Sichang privately promised to replace Liangyu with Renlong.
translations.idiomatic: He Renlong, meanwhile, had won repeated victories, and Sichang privately promised him Liangyu's post.

sentences.zh: 及良玉奏瑪瑙山捷，嗣昌語人龍須後命。

translations.literal: When Liangyu memorialized the victory at Agate Mountain, Sichang told Renlong to await later orders.
translations.idiomatic: After Liangyu reported the Agate Mountain victory, Sichang told Renlong to wait for further orders.

sentences.zh: 人龍大恨，具以前語告良玉，良玉亦內恨。

translations.literal: Renlong hated this greatly and fully told Liangyu the earlier words; Liangyu also harbored inner resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong was furious and told Liangyu every word of the earlier promise; Liangyu nursed a bitter grudge in turn.

sentences.zh: 當獻忠之敗走也，追且及，遣其党馬元利操重寶啖良玉曰：「獻忠在，故公見重。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong was defeated and fleeing, pursuit nearly caught him; he sent his partisan Ma Yuanli bearing heavy treasure to tempt Liangyu, saying: [While Xianzhong lives, therefore the Lord is valued.
translations.idiomatic: As Xianzhong fled in defeat, pursuit all but overtook him; he sent his follower Ma Yuanli with a heavy bribe to Liangyu, saying, "As long as Xianzhong remains, you are valued.

sentences.zh: 公所部多殺掠，而閣部猜且專。

translations.literal: The Lord's troops have done much killing and plunder, while the grand secretary is suspicious and autocratic.
translations.idiomatic: Your men loot and kill heavily, and the Grand Secretary distrusts you and keeps you on a short leash.

sentences.zh: 無獻忠，即公滅不久矣。

translations.literal: Without Xianzhong, the Lord will be destroyed before long.
translations.idiomatic: Without Xianzhong, you will not last long either."

sentences.zh: 」良玉心動，縱之去。

translations.literal: ] Liangyu's heart was moved, and he let him go.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu wavered and let him escape.

sentences.zh: 監軍萬元吉知良玉跋扈不可使，勸嗣昌令前軍躡賊，後軍繼之，而身從間道出梓潼扼歸以俟濟師，嗣昌不用。

translations.literal: Supervising commander Wan Yuanji knew Liangyu was overbearing and could not be employed; he urged Sichang to have the vanguard press the bandits, the rear army follow, while he himself by a bypath exit Zitong to choke the return route and await crossing troops—Sichang did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising commander Wan Yuanji saw that Liangyu was too arrogant to command and urged Sichang to have the van press the rebels while the rear followed, while he himself slipped through bypaths to Zitong to block their retreat and wait for reinforcements; Sichang ignored him.

sentences.zh: 賊既入蜀之巴州，人龍兵噪而西歸。

translations.literal: Once the bandits had entered Bazhou in Shu, Renlong's troops clamored and returned west.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels entered Bazhou in Sichuan, Renlong's men mutinied and marched west for home.

sentences.zh: 召良玉兵合擊，九檄皆不至。

translations.literal: He summoned Liangyu's troops for a combined strike; nine dispatches all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Liangyu to join the attack, but nine orders brought no response.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，諸軍追賊開縣之黃陵城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year the various armies pursued the bandits to Huanglingcheng in Kaixian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year fourteen the allied armies pursued the rebels to Huanglingcheng in Kaixian.

sentences.zh: 參將劉士傑深入，所當披靡。

translations.literal: Assistant commander Liu Shijie went deep in; wherever he met the enemy they were swept aside.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant commander Liu Shijie pushed deep into the enemy line and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 獻忠登高望，見無秦人旗幟，而良玉兵前部無鬥志，獨士傑孤軍。

translations.literal: Xianzhong climbed high and looked; he saw no Qin men's banners, and Liangyu's troops in the front had no fighting will—only Shijie's lone army.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong climbed to a vantage point and saw no Shaanxi banners; Liangyu's leading units had no stomach for a fight, and only Shijie stood alone.

sentences.zh: 乃密選壯士潛行箐穀中，乘高大呼馳下，良玉兵先潰，總兵猛如虎潰圍出。

translations.literal: He then secretly chose stalwart men to steal through bamboo valleys, and riding the height shouted and charged down; Liangyu's troops collapsed first, and regional commander Meng Ruhu broke the encirclement and got out.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly picked strong men to creep through the ravines, then charged shouting from the heights; Liangyu's men broke first, and regional commander Meng Ruhu fought his way out of the trap.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌方悔不用元吉言，而獻忠已席捲出川，西絕新開驛置，楚、蜀消息中斷，遂以計紿入襄陽城。

translations.literal: Sichang was only then regretting not using Yuanji's words, while Xianzhong had already swept out of Shu, cut off the Xinkai postal stations to the west, and Chu and Shu communications were severed; he then by stratagem deceived his way into Xiangyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang was only then regretting that he had ignored Yuanji, but Xianzhong had already burst out of Sichuan, severed the Xinkai courier route to the west, and cut off news between Huguang and Sichuan; by a ruse he then tricked his way into Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 襄王被執，嗣昌不食卒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang was seized; Sichang ceased eating and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiang was taken captive, and Sichang starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 賊瀕死復縱，迄以亡國者，以良玉素驕蹇不用命故也。

translations.literal: The bandits, on the brink of death, were again released, and in the end brought the state's ruin—because Liangyu had long been proud and obstinate and would not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: That the rebels, all but destroyed, were let loose again and in the end brought down the dynasty was because Liangyu had always been proud, defiant, and insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 二月，詔良玉削職戴罪，平賊自贖。

translations.literal: In the second month an edict stripped Liangyu's office while he bore guilt, to pacify bandits and redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the throne demoted Liangyu but let him redeem himself by crushing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 五月，獻忠陷南陽，即攻沁陽破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Xianzhong took Nanyang, then at once attacked Qinyang and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xianzhong seized Nanyang and immediately stormed and took Qinyang.

sentences.zh: 良玉至南陽，賊遁去。

translations.literal: Liangyu reached Nanyang and the bandits fled away.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangyu reached Nanyang the rebels slipped away.

sentences.zh: 良玉不戢士，沁人脫於賊者，遇官軍無噍類。

translations.literal: Liangyu did not restrain his soldiers; Qinyang people who had escaped from bandits, meeting government troops, had not a mouthful left alive.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu would not discipline his men; refugees from Qinyang who fell in with the imperial army were slaughtered to the last.

sentences.zh: 既而獻忠陷鄖西，掠地至信陽，屢勝而驕。

translations.literal: Before long Xianzhong took Yuxi, plundered lands as far as Xinyang, and after repeated victories grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xianzhong seized Yuxi, raided as far as Xinyang, and grew reckless with repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 良玉乃從南陽進兵，復大破之，降其眾數萬。

translations.literal: Liangyu then advanced troops from Nanyang and again greatly defeated them, receiving the surrender of several tens of thousands of his host.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu marched out from Nanyang, routed him again, and accepted the surrender of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 獻忠中股，負重傷夜遁。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was struck in the thigh, bore heavy wounds, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong took a ball in the thigh, was badly wounded, and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 而是時，李自成方殘襄城，圍良玉於郾城，幾陷。

translations.literal: Yet at this time Li Zicheng was just ravaging Xiangcheng and besieging Liangyu at Yancheng, nearly taking him.
translations.idiomatic: About then Li Zicheng was sacking Xiangcheng and had Liangyu besieged at Yancheng, nearly capturing him.

sentences.zh: 會陝西總督汪喬年出關，自成乃輟圍，與喬年戰襄陽城外。

translations.literal: It happened that Shaanxi governor Wang Qiaonian came out through the pass; Zicheng then ceased the siege and fought Qiaonian outside Xiangyang's walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi governor Wang Qiaonian marched out through the pass, Zicheng lifted the siege and met him outside Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 喬年軍盡覆，良玉不能救。

translations.literal: Qiaonian's army was completely overthrown; Liangyu could not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaonian's army was wiped out, and Liangyu could not save him.

sentences.zh: 帝既斬賀人龍以肅軍攻，專倚良玉辦賊。

translations.literal: The emperor had already beheaded He Renlong to restore military discipline, and relied solely on Liangyu to handle the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already executed He Renlong to restore discipline and now relied on Liangyu alone to deal with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月，自成復圍開封，乃釋故尚書初薦良玉者侯恂於獄，起為督師，發帑金十五萬犒良玉營將士，激勸之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year Zicheng again besieged Kaifeng; the former minister who had first recommended Liangyu, Hou Xun, was released from prison, raised as Grand Secretary, and one hundred fifty thousand taels from the treasury were issued to reward Liangyu's camp officers and soldiers and urge them on.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year fifteen Zicheng again besieged Kaifeng; the court freed from prison Hou Xun, the former minister who had first backed Liangyu, made him Grand Secretary, and sent a hundred and fifty thousand taels of treasury silver to reward Liangyu's officers and men and spur them on.

sentences.zh: 良玉及虎大威、楊德政會師硃仙鎮，賊營西，官軍營北。

translations.literal: Liangyu together with Hu Dawei and Yang Dezheng united armies at Zhuxian Town; the bandits camped west, the government army north.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu joined Hu Dawei and Yang Dezheng at Zhuxian Town; the rebels camped to the west, the imperial army to the north.

sentences.zh: 良玉見賊勢盛，一夕拔營遁，眾軍望見皆潰。

translations.literal: Liangyu saw the bandits' force was strong; in one night he uprooted camp and fled, and the various armies, seeing it, all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how strong the rebels were, Liangyu broke camp one night and fled, and every unit that saw it melted away.

sentences.zh: 自成戒士卒待良玉兵過，從後擊之。

translations.literal: Zicheng warned the soldiers to wait until Liangyu's troops had passed, then strike from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng ordered his men to let Liangyu's column pass, then hit it from the rear.

sentences.zh: 官軍幸追者緩，疾馳八十里。

translations.literal: The government army, fortunate that pursuers were slow, galloped hard eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial troops, lucky that pursuit lagged, raced eighty li.

sentences.zh: 賊已於其前穿塹深廣各二尋，環繞百里，自成親率眾遮於後。

translations.literal: The bandits had already before them dug trenches two xun deep and wide, encircling a hundred li; Zicheng personally led the host to block from behind.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already cut ditches two xun deep and wide across a hundred-li arc ahead of them, while Zicheng himself barred the rear.

sentences.zh: 良玉兵大亂，下馬渡溝，僵僕溪穀中，趾其顛而過。

translations.literal: Liangyu's troops were in great disorder; they dismounted to cross the trenches, corpses piled in streams and valleys, stepping on their crowns to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu's army fell into chaos; men dismounted to cross the ditches, treading on the heaped dead in the streams and ravines to get across.

sentences.zh: 賊從而蹂之，軍大敗，棄馬騾萬匹，器械無算，良玉走襄陽。

translations.literal: The bandits followed and trampled them; the army was greatly defeated, abandoning ten thousand horses and mules and weapons beyond reckoning; Liangyu fled to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rode them down; the army was shattered, leaving ten thousand horses and mules and countless arms, and Liangyu fled to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 帝聞良玉敗，詔恂拒河圖賊，而令良玉以兵來會。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Liangyu was defeated and ordered Xun to hold the river and plot against the bandits, while commanding Liangyu to come with troops and join.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of Liangyu's defeat he ordered Hou Xun to hold the Yellow River line against the rebels and told Liangyu to march and join him.

sentences.zh: 良玉畏自成，遷延不至。

translations.literal: Liangyu feared Zicheng and delayed, not arriving.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu feared Zicheng and dragged his feet, never coming.

sentences.zh: 九月，開封以河決而亡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Kaifeng perished because the river burst its banks.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Kaifeng was destroyed when the Yellow River broke its dikes.

sentences.zh: 帝怒恂，罷其官，不能罪良玉也。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at Xun, dismissed his office, and could not punish Liangyu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath fell on Hou Xun, who was dismissed, but Liangyu went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 開封既亡，自成無所得，遽引兵西，謀拔襄陽為根本。

translations.literal: Kaifeng having already perished, Zicheng gained nothing and hastily led his army west, planning to seize Xiangyang as his base.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaifeng fell, Li Zicheng had won nothing for his trouble. He hurried west, intending to make Xiangyang his base.

sentences.zh: 時良玉壁樊城，大造戰艦，驅襄陽一郡人以實軍，諸降賊附之，有眾二十萬。

translations.literal: At that time Liangyu fortified Fancheng, built warships on a great scale, drove the people of the whole Xiangyang commandery to fill out his army, and all surrendered bandits attached themselves to him, with a host of two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu held Fancheng and built a large fleet. He pressed the entire Xiangyang region into service and took in surrendered rebels until his force numbered two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 然親軍愛將大半死，而降人不奉約束，良玉亦漸衰多病，不復能與自成角矣。

translations.literal: Yet his personal troops and favored generals were mostly dead, and the surrendered men did not observe discipline. Liangyu too gradually declined, was often ill, and could no longer contend with Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his veteran officers were dead, however, and the surrendered troops obeyed no one. Liangyu himself grew old and sickly and could no longer stand against Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 自成乘勝攻良玉，良玉退兵南岸，結水寨相持，以萬人扼淺洲。

translations.literal: Zicheng attacked Liangyu while the victory was fresh. Liangyu withdrew his army to the south bank, set up water camps to face him, and used ten thousand men to hold the shallows.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng pressed the attack. Liangyu pulled back to the south bank, entrenched in river camps, and posted ten thousand men at the ford.

sentences.zh: 賊兵十萬爭渡，不能遏。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand bandit soldiers strove to cross and could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand rebel troops forced the crossing; nothing could hold them back.

sentences.zh: 良玉乃宵遁，引其舟師，左步右騎而下。

translations.literal: Liangyu then fled by night, leading his fleet with infantry on the left and cavalry on the right downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu fled by night, his fleet descending the river with infantry on one bank and cavalry on the other.

sentences.zh: 至武昌，從楚王乞二十萬人餉，曰：「我為王保境。

translations.literal: Reaching Wuchang, he begged two hundred thousand taels of pay from the Prince of Chu, saying: "I will guard the realm for the prince.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuchang he asked the Prince of Chu for two hundred thousand taels in rations, saying, "I will defend your territory for you.

sentences.zh: 」王不應，良玉縱兵大掠，火光照江中。

translations.literal: " The prince did not agree. Liangyu loosed his troops on a great pillage, and firelight lit the river.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince refused. Liangyu then let his soldiers loot on a vast scale until the river glowed with fire.

sentences.zh: 宗室士民奔竄山谷，多為土寇所害。

translations.literal: Clansmen, gentry, and common people fled into the hills and valleys, and many were killed by local bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and townspeople fled into the hills, where many fell prey to local bandits.

sentences.zh: 驛傳道王揚基奪門出，良玉兵掠其貲，並及其子女。

translations.literal: Along the courier road the prince Yang Ji broke out through the gate and fled. Liangyu's soldiers plundered his goods and seized his sons and daughters as well.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yang Ji of Chu fled through the gate; Liangyu's men looted his property and seized his children.

sentences.zh: 自十二月二十四日抵武昌，至十六年正月中，兵始去。

translations.literal: From the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month when they reached Wuchang until the middle of the first month of the sixteenth year, the troops at last departed.
translations.idiomatic: They had arrived at Wuchang on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month and did not leave until the middle of the first month of Chongzhen 16.

sentences.zh: 居人登蛇山以望，叫呼更生，曰：「左兵過矣！

translations.literal: The inhabitants climbed Serpent Hill to look, cried out as if reborn, and said: "The Left troops have passed!
translations.idiomatic: People climbed Serpent Hill to watch and shouted for joy: "The Left troops are gone!

sentences.zh: 」良玉既東，自成遂陷承天，傍掠諸州縣。

translations.literal: " After Liangyu had gone east, Zicheng then took Chengtian and raided the surrounding prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Liangyu had moved east, Li Zicheng captured Chengtian and swept the neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 當是時，降兵叛卒率假左軍號恣剽掠，蘄州守將王允成為亂首，破建德，劫池陽，去蕪湖四十里，泊舟三山、荻港，漕艘鹽舶盡奪以載兵。

translations.literal: At that time surrendered soldiers and mutinous troops mostly took the name of the Left Army and plundered at will. Wang Yuncheng, defending general of Qizhou, was the ringleader of the disorder. He broke Jiande, raided Chiyang, went within forty li of Wuhu, and moored boats at Sanshan and Digang. Grain transports and salt junks were all seized to carry troops.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered troops and mutineers everywhere marched under the banner of the Left Army. Wang Yuncheng, garrison commander of Qizhou, led them in sacking Jiande and Chiyang, advancing to within forty li of Wuhu and anchoring at Sanshan and Digang, where they seized grain barges and salt ships for transport.

sentences.zh: 聲言諸將寄帑南京，請以親信三千人與俱。

translations.literal: They declared that the generals had deposited funds in Nanjing and asked that three thousand trusted men be sent with them.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed the generals had stored treasure in Nanjing and demanded three thousand trusted men to accompany them there.

sentences.zh: 南京諸文武官及操江都御史至陳師江上為守禦。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of Nanjing and the censor-in-chief of river defense, Chen Shi, went to the river to organize defense.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's civil and military officials, together with river-defense censor Chen Shi, took up positions on the Yangtze to resist them.

sentences.zh: 士民一夕數徙，商旅不行。

translations.literal: Gentry and common people moved several times in a single night; merchants and travelers did not travel.
translations.idiomatic: Families fled their homes night after night, and the roads fell silent.

sentences.zh: 都御史李邦華被召，道湖口，草檄告良玉，以危詞動之。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Li Banghua was summoned. Passing Hukou, he drafted a proclamation to Liangyu and moved him with words of peril.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Banghua was recalled to court. At Hukou he drafted an urgent appeal to Liangyu, warning him of disaster.

sentences.zh: 而令安慶巡撫發九江庫銀十五萬兩，補六月糧，軍心乃定。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Anqing grand coordinator to issue one hundred fifty thousand taels from the Jiujiang treasury to cover the sixth month's rations, and the army's hearts were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged for the Anqing governor to release one hundred fifty thousand taels from the Jiujiang treasury for June's pay, and the troops calmed down.

sentences.zh: 邦華入見帝，論良玉潰兵之罪，請歸罪於王允成。

translations.literal: Banghua entered to see the emperor and discussed Liangyu's crime in letting his army dissolve, asking that guilt be laid on Wang Yuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Banghua reached court he blamed Liangyu for the mutiny and urged that Wang Yuncheng bear the punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令良玉誅允成，而獎其能定變。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Liangyu to execute Yuncheng and rewarded him for being able to quell the disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Liangyu to kill Wang Yuncheng but praised him for restoring order.

sentences.zh: 良玉卒留允成於軍中，不誅也。

translations.literal: Liangyu in the end kept Yuncheng in the army and did not execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu kept Wang Yuncheng in his ranks and never carried out the sentence.

sentences.zh: 良玉留安慶久之，徐溯九江上。

translations.literal: Liangyu remained in Anqing a long time, then slowly went upriver to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu lingered at Anqing, then slowly moved up the Yangtze toward Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 聞獻忠破湖廣，沉楚王于江，坐視不救。

translations.literal: He heard that Xianzhong had broken Huguang and drowned the Prince of Chu in the river, yet sat by and did not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: He learned that Zhang Xianzhong had overrun Huguang and drowned the Prince of Chu, yet he did nothing to save him.

sentences.zh: 八月乃入武昌，立軍府招徠，下流粗定，分命副將吳學禮援袁州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he at last entered Wuchang, set up a military headquarters to recruit men, and the lower reaches were roughly settled. He ordered the vice general Wu Xueli to relieve Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he finally reoccupied Wuchang, opened a headquarters to recruit troops, and brought a measure of calm to the lower Yangtze. He sent Vice General Wu Xueli to relieve Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 江西巡撫郭都賢惡其淫掠，檄歸之，而自募土人為戍守。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi grand coordinator Guo Duxian hated his rapine and plunder and ordered him recalled, himself recruiting locals for garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi governor Guo Duxian, disgusted by the army's depredations, ordered Liangyu back and raised local militia to hold the province.

sentences.zh: 會賊陷長沙、吉州，復陷袁州、岳州，良玉遣馬進忠援袁州，馬士秀援岳州。

translations.literal: When bandits took Changsha and Jizhou and again took Yuanzhou and Yuezhou, Liangyu sent Ma Jinzhong to relieve Yuanzhou and Ma Shixiu to relieve Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels seized Changsha, Jizhou, Yuanzhou, and Yuezhou, Liangyu dispatched Ma Jinzhong to Yuanzhou and Ma Shixiu to Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 士秀率水師敗賊岳州城下，二城遂並復。

translations.literal: Shixiu led the river force and defeated the bandits below Yuezhou city, and the two cities were both recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu routed the rebels on the water below Yuezhou, and both cities were retaken.

sentences.zh: 時帝命兵部侍郎呂大器代侯恂為總督，恂解任，中道逮下獄。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor ordered the vice minister of war Lü Daqi to replace Hou Xun as supreme commander. Xun was relieved of his post and on the road was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Vice Minister of War Lü Daqi to replace Hou Xun as supreme commander. Hou Xun was dismissed and arrested on his way home.

sentences.zh: 良玉知其為己故，心鞅鞅，與大器齟齬。

translations.literal: Liangyu knew it was on his account and was discontented at heart, and he was at odds with Daqi.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu knew Hou Xun had fallen because of him and resented Lü Daqi.

sentences.zh: 賊連陷建昌諸府，大器無兵不能救，良玉亦不援。

translations.literal: Bandits took Jianchang and other prefectures in succession. Daqi had no troops and could not save them, and Liangyu also did not aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels overran Jianchang and neighboring prefectures. Lü Daqi had no forces to send, and Liangyu offered no help.

sentences.zh: 進忠與賊戰嘉魚，再失利，良玉軍遂不振。

translations.literal: Jinzhong fought the bandits at Jiayu and twice met defeat. Liangyu's army then did not recover its vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jinzhong fought twice at Jiayu and lost both times. Liangyu's army never regained its edge.

sentences.zh: 會獻忠從荊河入蜀，良玉遣兵追之，距荊州七十里。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong entered Shu by the Jing River, Liangyu sent troops in pursuit, seventy li from Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xianzhong marched into Sichuan by the Jing River, Liangyu pursued him to within seventy li of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄諸賊因自成入關，盡懈。

translations.literal: The bandits of Jing and Xiang, because Zicheng had entered the Pass, all slackened.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Zicheng gone through the Pass into the north, the rebel bands of Jing and Xiang grew lax.

sentences.zh: 良玉偵知，乃遣副將盧光祖上隨、棗、承德，而惠登相自均、房，劉洪起自南陽，掎賊後，收其空虛地以自為功。

translations.literal: Liangyu learned of it by reconnaissance and then sent the vice general Lu Guangzu up through Sui, Zao, and Chengde, while Huidengxiang came from Jun and Fang and Liu Hongqi from Nanyang, to pinch the bandits from behind and seize their empty territory for his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu sent scouts, then dispatched Lu Guangzu north through Sui, Zao, and Chengde while Huidengxiang advanced from Jun and Fang and Liu Hongqi from Nanyang, striking empty rebel-held lands from the rear to pad his own record.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，詔封良玉為甯南伯，畀其子夢庚平賊將軍印，功成世守武昌。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year an edict enfeoffed Liangyu as Earl of Ningnan, gave his son Menggeng the seal of Pacifying-Bandits General, and on success he was to hold Wuchang in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chongzhen 17 the court made Liangyu Earl of Ningnan, gave his son Menggeng the seal of Pacifying-Bandits General, and promised that on victory Wuchang would be his family's hereditary seat.

sentences.zh: 命給事中左懋第便道督戰，良玉乃條日月進兵狀以聞。

translations.literal: He was ordered to give the supervising secretary Zuo Maodi authority to oversee the campaign on his route, and Liangyu then submitted a schedule of monthly advances.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zuo Maodi was sent to supervise the campaign en route, and Liangyu submitted a month-by-month plan of advance.

sentences.zh: 疏入，未奉旨，聞京師被陷，諸將洶洶，以江南自立君，請引兵東下。

translations.literal: The memorial had entered but the imperial rescript had not yet arrived when word came that the capital had fallen. The generals were in uproar and asked to move east, set up a ruler in Jiangnan, and lead the army downriver.
translations.idiomatic: Before the throne replied, news arrived that Beijing had fallen. His officers clamored to march east, crown a prince in the south, and descend the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 良玉慟哭，誓不許。

translations.literal: Liangyu wept bitterly and swore he would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu wept and swore he would never permit it.

sentences.zh: 副將士秀奮曰：「有不奉公令復言東下者，吾擊之！

translations.literal: The vice general Shixiu roused himself and said: "Whoever again speaks of going east without obeying the lord's order—I will strike him!
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Shixiu declared, "Anyone who speaks of marching east against the commander's order—I will kill him!

sentences.zh: 」以巨艦置砲斷江，眾乃定。

translations.literal: " They placed great ships with cannon to block the river, and the host was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: " They lined the river with heavy ships and cannon, and the army quieted down.

sentences.zh: 福王立，晉良玉為侯，廕一子錦衣衛正千戶，且並封黃得功、高傑、劉澤清、劉良佐為諸鎮，俱廕子世襲，而以上流之事專委良玉，尋加太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was established, Liangyu was advanced to marquis, one son was ennobled as hereditary chief of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard at the first rank, and Huang Degong, Gao Jie, Liu Zeqing, and Liu Liangzuo were all enfeoffed as frontier commanders, their sons likewise ennobled in succession. Affairs of the upper reaches were entrusted solely to Liangyu, and he was soon made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongguang regime was proclaimed, Liangyu was made a marquis and his son ennobled in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
