Huang Degong, Gao Jie, Liu Zeqing, and Liu Liangzuo were enfeoffed as regional commanders with hereditary honors for their sons. The court left the entire upper Yangtze to Liangyu and soon named him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時李自成敗於關門，良玉得以其間稍復楚西境之荊州、德安、承天。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng had been defeated at Shanhaiguan, and Liangyu was able in the interval to recover somewhat the western Huguang prefectures of Jingzhou, De'an, and Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had just been broken at Shanhaiguan, and in the breathing space Liangyu recovered parts of western Huguang—Jingzhou, De'an, and Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 而湖廣巡撫何騰蛟及總督袁繼咸居江西，皆與良玉善，南都倚為遮罩。

translations.literal: The Huguang grand coordinator He Tengjiao and the supreme commander Yuan Jixian were in Jiangxi, both on good terms with Liangyu, and the Southern Capital relied on them as a screen.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang governor He Tengjiao and supreme commander Yuan Jixian in Jiangxi were both friendly with Liangyu, and Nanjing counted on them as its shield.

sentences.zh: 良玉兵八十萬，號百萬，前五營為親軍，後五營為降軍。

translations.literal: Liangyu's army was eight hundred thousand, called a million. The first five camps were his personal army; the last five were surrendered troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu commanded eight hundred thousand men on paper—a million, he claimed. The first five camps were his household troops; the last five were surrendered rebels.

sentences.zh: 每春秋肄兵武昌諸山，一山幟一色，山谷為滿。

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn he drilled troops on the hills around Wuchang. One hill, one banner color—the valleys were full.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn he held grand reviews on the hills around Wuchang, one peak per banner color until the valleys brimmed with flags.

sentences.zh: 軍法用兩人夾馬馳，曰：「過對」。

translations.literal: Military law used two men flanking a galloping horse, called out: "Pass in pairs."
translations.idiomatic: Drill law required pairs of riders to gallop past each other, crying, "Pass in pairs!"

sentences.zh: 馬足動地殷如雷，聲聞數里。

translations.literal: Hoofbeats shook the ground like thunder, audible for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Hoofbeats shook the earth like thunder and could be heard for miles.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮兵惟高傑最強，不及良玉遠甚。

translations.literal: Among the frontier commanders' troops only Gao Jie's were strongest, yet they fell far short of Liangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the regional armies Gao Jie's was the strongest—and still no match for Liangyu.

sentences.zh: 然良玉自硃仙鎮之敗，精銳略盡，其後歸者多烏合，軍容雖壯，法令不復相懾。

translations.literal: Yet since Liangyu's defeat at Zhuxian Town his crack troops were nearly gone. Those who returned afterward were mostly a rabble. Though the army's appearance was imposing, the laws no longer awed them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhuxianzhen, however, his elite were gone. What remained was mostly rabble. The host looked magnificent, but discipline had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 良玉家殲于許州，其在武昌，諸營優娼歌舞達旦，良玉塊然獨處，無姬侍。

translations.literal: Liangyu's family was wiped out at Xuzhou. In Wuchang the camps had actors and singing girls reveling until dawn, while Liangyu sat alone, without concubines in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been slaughtered at Xuzhou. In Wuchang his camps caroused with actors and courtesans until dawn while he sat alone without a woman near him.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜宴僚佐，召營妓十餘人行酒，履濆交錯，少焉左顧而欬，以次引出。

translations.literal: Once at a night feast for his staff he summoned more than ten camp courtesans to pour wine. Footgear splashed and crossed; presently he looked left and coughed, and they were led out in turn.
translations.idiomatic: At a midnight banquet for his staff he called in a dozen camp courtesans to pour wine. When slippers began to tangle under the table he glanced aside and coughed, and they were led out one by one.

sentences.zh: 賓客肅然，左右莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: The guests were solemn; those at his side did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: The guests sat in silence; no one beside him dared raise his eyes.

sentences.zh: 其統馭有體，為下所服多此類。

translations.literal: His command had form and was obeyed below in many such ways.
translations.idiomatic: In such ways he still commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 而是時，良玉已老且病，無中原意矣。

translations.literal: Yet by then Liangyu was old and ill and had no mind for the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: By then, however, he was old, sick, and had lost any ambition for the north.

sentences.zh: 良玉之起由侯恂。

translations.literal: Liangyu's rise had come through Hou Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu owed his career to Hou Xun.

sentences.zh: 恂，故東林也。

translations.literal: Xun was of the old Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xun belonged to the Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 馬士英、阮大鋮用事，慮東林倚良玉為難，謾語修好，而陰忌之，築板磯城為西防。

translations.literal: Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng held power, feared the Donglin would rely on Liangyu to make trouble, spoke falsely of restoring good relations, yet secretly resented him and built the Banji fortress as a western defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng, fearing the Donglin might use Liangyu against them, made show of friendship while secretly building the fortress at Banji to block him from the west.

sentences.zh: 良玉歎曰：「今西何所防，殆防我耳。

translations.literal: Liangyu sighed and said: "What is there to defend on the west now? I fear they are defending against me.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu sighed. "What enemy lies to the west now? They are building that wall against me.

sentences.zh: 」會朝事日非，監軍御史黃澍挾良玉勢，面觸馬、阮。

translations.literal: " When court affairs daily worsened, the supervising censor Huang Shu relied on Liangyu's power and openly confronted Ma and Ruan.
translations.idiomatic: " As Nanjing politics rotted, supervising censor Huang Shu, backed by Liangyu, openly defied Ma and Ruan.

sentences.zh: 既返，遣緹騎逮澍，良玉留澍不遣。

translations.literal: After he returned, the court sent imperial guards to arrest Shu. Liangyu detained Shu and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Shu returned east, the court sent agents to arrest him. Liangyu held him back.

sentences.zh: 澍與諸將日以清君側為請，良玉躊躇弗應。

translations.literal: Shu and the generals daily asked to purge the court of evil ministers, but Liangyu hesitated and did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and the generals daily urged a purge of the court; Liangyu wavered and refused.

sentences.zh: 亡何，有北來太子事，澍借此激眾以報己怨，召三十六營大將與之盟。

translations.literal: Before long there was the affair of the crown prince from the north. Shu used this to stir the host to avenge his own grievance and summoned the thirty-six camp generals to swear an oath with him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon came rumors of a northern crown prince. Huang Shu seized on them to rouse the army for his private revenge and summoned the thirty-six camp commanders to swear an oath.

sentences.zh: 良玉反意乃決，傳檄討馬士英，自漢口達蘄州，列舟二百餘里。

translations.literal: Liangyu's intent to rebel was then fixed. He issued a proclamation denouncing Ma Shiying, from Hankou reaching Qizhou, with boats lined up for more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu's rebellion was set. He issued a manifesto against Ma Shiying, and his fleet stretched two hundred li from Hankou to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 良玉疾已劇，至九江，邀總督袁繼咸入舟中，袖中出密諭，雲自皇太子，劫諸將盟，繼鹹正辭拒之。

translations.literal: Liangyu's illness had already grown severe. Reaching Jiujiang, he invited the supreme commander Yuan Jixian into his boat, took a secret edict from his sleeve said to be from the true crown prince, and forced the generals to swear an oath. Jixian sternly refused in proper words.
translations.idiomatic: His illness was grave. At Jiujiang he invited Yuan Jixian aboard, produced a secret edict he claimed came from the true crown prince, and tried to bind the generals by oath. Yuan Jixian refused in the clearest terms.

sentences.zh: 部將郝效忠陰入城，縱火殘其城而去。

translations.literal: The divisional general Hao Xiaozhong secretly entered the city, set fires, ravaged the city, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Divisional general Hao Xiaozhong slipped into the city, set it ablaze, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 良玉望城中火光，曰：「予負袁公。

translations.literal: Liangyu looked at the firelight in the city and said: "I have wronged Master Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Watching the flames, Liangyu said, "I have betrayed Master Yuan.

sentences.zh: 」嘔血數升，是夜死。

translations.literal: " He vomited several sheng of blood and died that night.
translations.idiomatic: " He coughed up a great quantity of blood and died that night.

sentences.zh: 時順治二年四月也。

translations.literal: It was the fourth month of the second year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: It was the fourth month of Shunzhi 2—1645.

sentences.zh: 諸將秘不發喪，共推其子夢庚為留後。

translations.literal: The generals kept his death secret and jointly made his son Menggeng acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: The generals hid his death and installed his son Menggeng as acting commander.

sentences.zh: 七日，軍東下，朝命黃得功渡江防剿。

translations.literal: On the seventh day the army went east. The court ordered Huang Degong to cross the river to intercept and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later the army marched east. The court ordered Huang Degong across the river to stop them.

sentences.zh: 初，夢庚自立，佯語繼咸至池州侯旨。

translations.literal: At first, when Menggeng had set himself up, he pretended to tell Jixian to come to Chizhou and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Menggeng first took command he told Yuan Jixian to meet him at Chizhou for instructions.

sentences.zh: 抵池，繼鹹密以疏聞，道梗不得達。

translations.literal: On reaching the pool, Jixian secretly sent up a memorial, but the roads were blocked and it could not reach the court.
translations.idiomatic: At Chizhou, Yuan Jixian secretly memorialized the throne, but the roads were cut and the dispatch never arrived.

sentences.zh: 惠登相者，初為賊，既降，為良玉副將。

translations.literal: Huidengxiang had at first been a bandit; after surrendering he became Liangyu's vice general.
translations.idiomatic: Huidengxiang had begun as a rebel; after surrendering he became one of Liangyu's vice generals.

sentences.zh: 諸軍自彭澤下，連陷建德、東流，殘安慶城，獨池州不破，貽書登相曰：「留此以待後軍。

translations.literal: The armies went down from Pengze, took Jiande and Dongliu in succession, ravaged Anqing city, and only Chizhou was not taken. They sent a letter to Huidengxiang saying: "Leave this to await the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: The host descended from Pengze, sacked Jiande and Dongliu, wrecked Anqing, and spared only Chizhou, writing Huidengxiang, "Hold this place for the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 」登相大詬曰：「若此，則我反不如前為流賊時矣，如先帥末命何！

translations.literal: " Huidengxiang cursed loudly and said: "If it is like this, then I am not even as good as when I was a roaming bandit before. What of the late commander's last charge!
translations.idiomatic: " Huidengxiang raged: "If this is how you fight, I was nobler as a bandit. What of our dead lord's last command!

sentences.zh: 」檄其軍返。

translations.literal: " He ordered his army to return.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned his troops back.

sentences.zh: 夢庚見黑旗船西上，索輕舸追及之，登相與相見大慟。

translations.literal: Menggeng saw black-flag boats going upriver west and sought light craft to overtake them. Huidengxiang met him and they wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Menggeng saw black-banner ships heading west, took a light boat in pursuit, and met Huidengxiang in a storm of tears.

sentences.zh: 以夢庚不足事，引兵絕江而去，諸將乃議旋師。

translations.literal: Holding that Menggeng was not worth serving, he led his army across the river and left. The generals then discussed turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Deciding Menggeng was unworthy, Huidengxiang crossed the Yangtze and marched away, and the other generals began to talk of retreat.

sentences.zh: 時大清兵已下泗州，逼儀真矣。

translations.literal: At that time the Great Qing army had already taken Sizhou and was pressing Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Qing army had taken Sizhou and was closing on Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 夢庚遂偕澍以眾降於九江。

translations.literal: Menggeng then went with Shu and the host to surrender at Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Menggeng then surrendered at Jiujiang with Huang Shu and the whole army.

sentences.zh: 鄧，四川人。

translations.literal: Deng, a man of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan was a native of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，從軍，積功得守備。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he joined the army and through accumulated merit became a garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he entered military service and rose by merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 安邦彥反，追賊織金，勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: An Bangyan rebelled, and  pursued the bandits to Zhijin, his courage ranking first among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: When An Bangyan rebelled, Deng Yan pursued the rebels to Zhijin with a valor that outshone every other commander.

sentences.zh: 已，敗織績河濱。

translations.literal: Afterward he was defeated at the Zhiji River bank.
translations.idiomatic: He was later defeated on the banks of the Zhiji River.

sentences.zh: 魯欽敗歿，賊犯威清。

translations.literal: Lu Qin was defeated and killed, and the bandits invaded Weiqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qin was defeated and killed, the rebels invaded Weiqing.

sentences.zh: 夜斫營走賊，進都司僉書。

translations.literal:  by night cut the camp and drove off the bandits, and was promoted to assistant commander in the capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan raided the rebel camp by night and drove them off, earning promotion to assistant commander in the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 討敗苗酋李阿二。

translations.literal: He campaigned and defeated the Miao chieftain Li A'er.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against and defeated the Miao chieftain Li A'er.

sentences.zh: 自貴州用兵，裨將楊明楷、劉志敏、張雲鵬並驍勇，不得為大將，惟以功名聞。

translations.literal: From the time troops were used in Guizhou, the vice generals Yang Mingkai, Liu Zhimin, and Zhang Yunpeng were all fierce and brave yet could not become great generals; only  was known for merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guizhou campaigns, vice generals Yang Mingkai, Liu Zhimin, and Zhang Yunpeng were all fierce fighters who never won high command; only Deng Yan won fame for real achievement.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，屢遷四川副總兵，與侯良柱共斬安邦彥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was repeatedly promoted to vice commander-in-chief of Sichuan and with Hou Liangzhu jointly beheaded An Bangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he rose to Sichuan vice commander-in-chief and, with Hou Liangzhu, jointly beheaded An Bangyan.

sentences.zh: 京師有警，率六千人勤王，共復遵、永四城。

translations.literal: When the capital was in alarm he led six thousand men to relieve the throne and together recovered the four cities of Zun and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When Beijing was threatened he marched six thousand men to the capital's aid and helped recover the four Zun and Yong cities.

sentences.zh: 加署都督僉事，世廕千戶。

translations.literal: He was given acting rank as vice commissioner-in-chief and hereditary ennoblement as a thousand-household in the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He received acting rank as vice commissioner-in-chief and hereditary ennoblement as a guard thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 尋擢總兵官，鎮守遵化。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to commander-in-chief and garrisoned Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made full commander-in-chief and posted to garrison Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 戰喜峰口及洪山，並有功，進秩為真。

translations.literal: He fought at Xifengkou and Hongshan and had merit in both, and his rank was made substantive.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Xifengkou and Hongshan with distinction, and his rank was made substantive.

sentences.zh: 五年春，叛將亂登、萊，王洪等無功。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year rebel generals rioted in Deng and Lai; Wang Hong and others had no success.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year rebel generals mutinied in Dengzhou and Laizhou; Wang Hong and others accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 自請行，命為援剿總兵官，與洪及劉國柱禦賊沙河，戰相當。

translations.literal:  asked to go himself and was appointed Pacifying-Rebellion commander-in-chief. With Hong and Liu Guozhu he defended against the bandits at the Sha River and fought to a standstill.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan volunteered, was named Pacifying-Rebellion commander-in-chief, and with Wang Hong and Liu Guozhu held the rebels on the Sha River to a stalemate.

sentences.zh: 已而遁走，賊乘之，大敗。

translations.literal: Before long they fled, the bandits pursued them, and there was a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they broke and fled; the rebels chased them down for a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 尋與諸將金國奇等復登、萊二城，錄功進署都督同知。

translations.literal: Soon with the generals Jin Guoqi and others he recovered the two cities of Deng and Lai, and for the recorded merit he was advanced to acting commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Jin Guoqi and others in retaking Dengzhou and Laizhou and was promoted to acting commissioner-in-chief for the victory.

sentences.zh: 戍遵化久，思歸。

translations.literal:  garrisoned Zunhua a long time and longed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After long service at Zunhua, Deng Yan yearned to go home.

sentences.zh: 及登、萊事竣，復以為言。

translations.literal: When the Deng and Lai affair was finished, he again spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deng-Lai campaign ended, he petitioned once more to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 會賊入河北，言者請令剿，怏怏而行。

translations.literal: Just then the bandits entered Hebei; memorialists asked that  be ordered to suppress them, and  set out in sullen reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the rebels entered Hebei, and memorialists urged that Deng Yan be sent to suppress them; he marched off in sullen reluctance.

sentences.zh: 給事中範淑泰劾虐民，帝不問，旋遣近侍監其軍。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Fan Shutai impeached  for oppressing the people; the emperor made no inquiry, and soon sent a palace attendant to supervise his army.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Fan Shutai impeached Deng Yan for oppressing civilians, but the emperor took no notice and soon dispatched a palace attendant to supervise his army.

sentences.zh: 至濟源，射殺王自用于善陽山，即賊紫金梁也。

translations.literal:  reached Jiyuan and shot dead Wang Ziyong at Shanyang Mountain—he was the bandit Zijinliang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan reached Jiyuan and shot dead Wang Ziyong on Mount Shanyang—the rebel known as Zijinliang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，賊逼磁州，拒卻之彭城鎮。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits pressed Cizhou; he repulsed them at Pengcheng town.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels pressed Cizhou; he drove them back at Pengcheng Town.

sentences.zh: 與左良玉擊賊清池、柳莊，賊走林縣。

translations.literal: With Zuo Liangyu he struck the bandits at Qingchi and Liuzhuang; the bandits fled to Lin County.
translations.idiomatic: With Zuo Liangyu he attacked the rebels at Qingchi and Liuzhuang, and the rebels fled toward Lin County.

sentences.zh: 部將楊遇春邀賊，中伏死。

translations.literal: 's subordinate general Yang Yuchun intercepted the bandits and died in an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan's subordinate Yang Yuchun intercepted the rebels and was killed in an ambush.

sentences.zh: 賊用其旗，並誘殺他將，自是輕。

translations.literal: The bandits used his banners and also lured other generals to their deaths; from then on they held  in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels flew his banners and lured other commanders to their deaths as well; from then on they held Deng Yan in contempt.

sentences.zh: 俄與良玉逐賊沙河，賊圍湯陰，被困土樵窩，良玉救乃免。

translations.literal: Soon, with Liangyu, he pursued the bandits to the Sha River; the bandits besieged Tangyin,  was trapped at Tuchao Nest, and only Liangyu’s rescue freed him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Liangyu pursued the rebels to the Sha River; when the rebels besieged Tangyin, Deng Yan was trapped at Tuchao Nest and escaped only because Liangyu came to his rescue.

sentences.zh: 已，共破賊官村、沁河、清化、萬善，移師畿南，敗賊白草關。

translations.literal: Afterward they together broke the bandits at Guancun, on the Qin River, at Qinghua, and at Wanshan, moved the army south of the capital region, and defeated the bandits at Baicao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: They then jointly defeated the rebels at Guancun, on the Qin River, at Qinghua, and at Wanshan, shifted the army to the south of the capital region, and beat the rebels at Baicao Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊犯平山，敗之紅子店、馬種川。

translations.literal: The bandits invaded Pingshan; he defeated them at Hongzi Shop and Machuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels invaded Pingshan, he defeated them at Hongzi Shop and Machuan.

sentences.zh: 賊遁青石嶺敗之紅澗村、醉漢口。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Qing Stone Ridge; he defeated them at Hongjian Village and Drunkard’s Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Qing Stone Ridge; he defeated them at Hongjian Village and Drunkard’s Mouth.

sentences.zh: 賊犯臨城，敗之魚桂嶺。

translations.literal: The bandits invaded Lincheng; he defeated them at Yugui Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels invaded Lincheng, he defeated them at Yugui Ridge.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊蔓河溯及畿南，天子特遣倪寵、王樸將京軍，而保定梁甫，河南左良玉，湯九州合軍足殄賊。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits spread along the river upstream and reached the region south of the capital; the Son of Heaven specially dispatched Ni Chong and Wang Pu to lead the capital army, while Liang Fu of Baoding, Zuo Liangyu of Henan, and Tang Jiuzhou together with ’s army were enough to exterminate the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebels had spread upriver into the region south of the capital. The emperor specially sent Ni Chong and Wang Pu with the capital army, while Liang Fu of Baoding, Zuo Liangyu of Henan, and Tang Jiuzhou together with Deng Yan’s forces were more than enough to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 群帥勢相軋，彼此觀望，托山深道岐以自解，莫利先入，賊遂由澠池南渡。

translations.literal: The commanders’ power checked one another; each watched the other, excusing himself with deep mountains and branching roads, and none wished to strike first—so the bandits crossed south from Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders checked one another’s power, each holding back and excusing delay with rugged terrain and winding roads, unwilling to strike first; the rebels therefore crossed south from Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 而諸帥各有近侍為中軍，事易掩飾，所報功多不以實也。

translations.literal: Moreover, each commander had a palace attendant as his staff officer, so affairs were easily concealed and reported merit often did not match reality.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, each commander had a palace attendant on his staff, making cover-ups easy; the merit they reported often did not match reality.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊南遁，追敗之澠池扣子山，至宜陽、盧氏而還。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the bandits fled south;  pursued and defeated them at Kouzi Mountain in Mianchi, then returned after reaching Yiyang and Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the rebels fled south; Deng Yan pursued and defeated them at Kouzi Mountain in Mianchi, then withdrew after reaching Yiyang and Lushi.

sentences.zh: 是月以為保定總兵官，代梁甫。

translations.literal: That month  was made regional commander of Baoding, replacing Liang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Deng Yan was appointed regional commander of Baoding, replacing Liang Fu.

sentences.zh: 七年正月以賊盡入鄖、襄，命援剿，解南漳圍。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, because the bandits had all entered Yun and Xiang,  was ordered to reinforce the suppression and raise the siege of Nanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, with the rebels concentrated in Yun and Xiang, Deng Yan was ordered to reinforce the campaign and lift the siege of Nanzhang.

sentences.zh: 尋敗賊胡地沖，斬闖天王、九條龍、草上飛、抓山虎、雙翼虎。

translations.literal: Soon he defeated the bandits at Hudi Chong and beheaded Dash Heavenly King, Nine-Striped Dragon, Grass Skimmer, Mountain-Grasping Tiger, and Double-Winged Tiger.
translations.idiomatic: He soon defeated the rebels at Hudi Chong and beheaded Dash Heavenly King, Nine-Striped Dragon, Grass Skimmer, Mountain-Grasping Tiger, and Double-Winged Tiger.

sentences.zh: 剿房縣、竹山、南漳賊，戰獅子崖、石漳山，斬一隻虎、滿天飛。

translations.literal: He suppressed bandits in Fang County, Zhushan, and Nanzhang, fought at Lion Cliff and Shizhang Mountain, and beheaded One Tiger and Sky-Filling Flight.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed rebels in Fang, Zhushan, and Nanzhang, fought at Lion Cliff and Mount Shizhang, and killed One Tiger and Sky-Filling Flight.

sentences.zh: 已，擊賊洵陽乜家溝，連戰皆捷，獲首功一千有奇。

translations.literal: Afterward he struck the bandits at Yijia Gully in Xunyang; battle after battle was victorious, and more than a thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked the rebels at Yijia Gully in Xunyang; victory followed victory, and more than a thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 八月敘五峰山破賊功，進右都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the merit of breaking bandits at Wufeng Mountain, he was advanced to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month his victory over the rebels at Wufeng Mountain was entered on the merit rolls and he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 不善馭軍，軍心亦不附，噪於鄖西，渡河以避之，總督陳奇瑜犒慰乃定。

translations.literal:  was not skilled at controlling troops, and the army’s heart did not attach to him; they mutinied west of Yun, and  crossed the river to avoid them—only after Governor Chen Qiyu comforted them with rewards did they settle.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan was a poor disciplinarian and his men were not loyal to him; they mutinied west of Yun, and he crossed the river to escape them—only after Governor Chen Qiyu pacified them with rewards did the uproar subside.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜集諸將討竹山、竹溪諸賊，頻有功。

translations.literal: Qiyu gathered the generals to suppress bandits in Zhushan, Zhuxi, and other places, and  repeatedly won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu gathered the generals to suppress rebels in Zhushan, Zhuxi, and elsewhere, and Deng Yan won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊大入河南，命援剿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the bandits made a great incursion into Henan, and  was ordered to reinforce the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the rebels poured into Henan in force, and Deng Yan was ordered to reinforce the campaign.

sentences.zh: 八年春，賊陷新蔡，知縣王信罵賊死，追敗賊 羅山。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year the bandits took Xincai; Magistrate Wang Xin cursed the bandits and died.  pursued and defeated the bandits at Luoshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year the rebels captured Xincai; Magistrate Wang Xin cursed them and was killed. Deng Yan pursued and defeated the rebels at Luoshan.

sentences.zh: 是時，賊陷鳳陽，命自黃州速援安慶。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits took Fengyang, and  was ordered to hurry from Huangzhou to relieve Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebels had taken Fengyang, and Deng Yan was ordered to hurry from Huangzhou to relieve Anqing.

sentences.zh: 及桐城被圍，竟不至。

translations.literal: When Tongcheng was besieged, he in the end did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongcheng came under siege, he never arrived.

sentences.zh: 御史錢守廉劾剿賊羅山，殺良冒功，命總督洪承疇核之。

translations.literal: Censor Qian Shoulian impeached  for suppressing bandits at Luoshan while killing the innocent and claiming merit; the emperor ordered Governor Hong Chengchou to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qian Shoulian impeached Deng Yan for killing civilians and claiming merit while campaigning at Luoshan; the emperor ordered Governor Hong Chengchou to investigate.

sentences.zh: 四月，承疇至汝州，令戍樊城，防漢江。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Chengchou reached Ruzhou and ordered  to garrison Fancheng and guard the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chengchou reached Ruzhou and ordered Deng Yan to garrison Fancheng and guard the Han River.

sentences.zh: 是月，部將王允成以克餉鼓噪，殺其二僕。

translations.literal: That month his subordinate Wang Yuncheng raised a mutiny over withheld pay and killed two of his servants.
translations.idiomatic: That month his subordinate Wang Yuncheng mutinied over withheld pay and killed two of his servants.

sentences.zh: 懼，登樓越牆墮地死。

translations.literal:  was afraid, climbed a tower, leaped over the wall, fell to the ground, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Deng Yan climbed a tower, leaped over the wall, fell to the ground, and died.

sentences.zh: 由小校，大小數百戰，所向克捷。

translations.literal:  rose from a petty officer; in several hundred battles large and small, wherever he went he won.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan had risen from the ranks; in several hundred engagements large and small, he had been victorious wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 以久戍觖望，恣其下淫掠。

translations.literal: Because of long garrison service he nursed resentment, and he let his men rape and plunder at will.
translations.idiomatic: After long years on garrison duty he grew resentful and let his men rape and plunder at will.

sentences.zh: 大學士王應熊以鄉里庇之，益無所憚。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Yingxiong shielded him as a fellow townsman, and  grew ever more fearless.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Yingxiong shielded him as a fellow townsman, and Deng Yan grew ever more brazen.

sentences.zh: 其死也，人以為逸罰雲。

translations.literal: At his death people thought he had escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, people said he had escaped the punishment he deserved.

sentences.zh: 賀人龍，米脂人。

translations.literal: He Renlong was a man of Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: He Renlong was a native of Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 初以守備隸延綏巡撫洪承疇麾下。

translations.literal: At first, as garrison commander, he served under Yan-sui governor Hong Chengchou.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as garrison commander under Yan-sui governor Hong Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，承疇受賊降，命人龍勞以酒，伏兵擊斬三百二十人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, Chengchou accepted the bandits’ surrender and ordered Renlong to entertain them with wine; concealed troops struck and beheaded three hundred twenty men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, Chengchou accepted rebel surrenders and ordered Renlong to entertain them with wine while concealed troops struck and killed three hundred twenty men.

sentences.zh: 其冬，張福臻代承疇，遣人龍剿賊黨雄，斬獲二百有奇。

translations.literal: That winter Zhang Fuzhen replaced Chengchou and sent Renlong to suppress the bandit Dang Xiong; beheadings and captures exceeded two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhang Fuzhen replaced Chengchou and sent Renlong against the rebel Dang Xiong; beheadings and captures exceeded two hundred.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，從福臻擒賊孫守法。

translations.literal: The next summer he followed Fuzhen in capturing the bandit Sun Shoufa.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he followed Fuzhen in capturing the rebel Sun Shoufa.

sentences.zh: 其秋，以所部援剿山西。

translations.literal: That autumn he led his command to Shanxi on reinforcement duty.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he led his command into Shanxi on reinforcement duty.

sentences.zh: 六年春，與總兵尤世祿復遼州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he and Regional Commander You Shilu recovered Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he and regional commander You Shilu recovered Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 已，敗賊垣曲、絳縣。

translations.literal: Afterward he defeated bandits at Yuanqu and Jiang County.
translations.idiomatic: He then defeated rebels at Yuanqu and Jiang County.

sentences.zh: 進都司僉書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Commander in the Capital Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant commander in the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 又連破賊水頭鎮、花池塞、湯湖村。

translations.literal: He again broke bandits at Shuitou town, Huachi stockade, and Tanghu village.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated rebels at Shuitou Town, Huachi Stockade, and Tanghu Village.

sentences.zh: 會山西賊幾盡，乃還陝西。

translations.literal: When Shanxi bandits were nearly exhausted, he returned to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shanxi rebels were nearly wiped out, he returned to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 從巡撫陳奇瑜討平延川賊，浮斬一千有奇。

translations.literal: Following Governor Chen Qiyu he pacified the Yanchuan bandits and beheaded more than a thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under Governor Chen Qiyu he pacified the Yanchuan rebels and beheaded more than a thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜擢總督，以人龍自隨。

translations.literal: Qiyu was promoted to governor-general and took Renlong with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiyu was promoted to governor-general, Renlong accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 七年四月擊賊隰州，擒克天虎，進參將。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year he struck bandits at Xizhou and captured Ke Tianhu, and was advanced to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventh year he attacked rebels at Xizhou, captured Ke Tianhu, and was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜追賊鄖、襄、興、漢，人龍並有功。

translations.literal: Qiyu pursued bandits through Yun, Xiang, Xing, and Han; Renlong won merit throughout.
translations.idiomatic: As Qiyu pursued rebels through Yun, Xiang, Xing, and Han, Renlong won merit throughout.

sentences.zh: 賊軼車箱峽，陷隴州西去，奇瑜遣人龍救之。

translations.literal: The bandits slipped through Chexiang Gorge and, having taken Longzhou, went west; Qiyu sent Renlong to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped through Chexiang Gorge, took Longzhou, and marched west; Qiyu sent Renlong to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 甫入隴州，李自成復至，環攻。

translations.literal: He had just entered Longzhou when Li Zicheng came again and besieged it in a ring.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely entered Longzhou when Li Zicheng returned and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 以人龍同里閈，遣其將高傑移書令反，人龍不報。

translations.literal: Because Renlong was a fellow townsman, Li sent his general Gao Jie with a letter urging him to defect; Renlong did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Li, knowing Renlong was a fellow townsman, sent his general Gao Jie with a letter urging defection; Renlong did not reply.

sentences.zh: 固守兩月，左光先救至，圍始解。

translations.literal: He held firm for two months; when Zuo Guangxian’s relief arrived, the siege was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He held out for two months until Zuo Guangxian’s relief arrived and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 十二月敗賊中莊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he defeated bandits at Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he defeated rebels at Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，鳳陽陷，總督洪承疇遣人龍馳救，敗賊睢州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Fengyang fell; Governor-General Hong Chengchou sent Renlong to the rescue at full speed, and he defeated bandits at Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Fengyang fell; Governor-General Hong Chengchou sent Renlong to the rescue at full speed, and he defeated rebels at Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 進副總兵。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 承疇以陝西急，率人龍入關。

translations.literal: Chengchou, because Shaanxi was urgent, led Renlong through the passes into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: With Shaanxi in crisis, Chengchou led Renlong through the passes into the interior.

sentences.zh: 商、洛賊馬光玉等薄西安，距大軍五十里。

translations.literal: The Shang and Luo bandits Ma Guangyu and others pressed close to Xi’an, fifty li from the main army.
translations.idiomatic: The Shang and Luo rebels Ma Guangyu and others pressed Xi’an, coming within fifty li of the main army.

sentences.zh: 承疇命人龍入子午穀，邀賊之南；

translations.literal: Chengchou ordered Renlong to enter Ziwu Valley and intercept the bandits from the south;
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou ordered Renlong into Ziwu Valley to intercept the rebels from the south;

sentences.zh: 別將劉成功、王永祥邀賊之北；

translations.literal: other generals Liu Chenggong and Wang Yongxiang were to intercept them from the north;
translations.idiomatic: other generals Liu Chenggong and Wang Yongxiang were to intercept them from the north;

sentences.zh: 張全昌從咸陽繞興平東。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanchang was to circle east from Xianyang through Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanchang was to swing east from Xianyang through Xingping.

sentences.zh: 賊以此不敢南遁，盡走武功、扶風，又渡渭走郿縣。

translations.literal: The bandits therefore dared not flee south; they all went to Wugong and Fufeng, then crossed the Wei and fled to Mei County.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels therefore dared not flee south; they all went to Wugong and Fufeng, then crossed the Wei and fled to Mei County.

sentences.zh: 承疇追至王渠鎮，賊方掠南山。

translations.literal: Chengchou pursued to Wangqu town; the bandits were then plundering the southern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou pursued to Wangqu Town while the rebels were plundering the southern hills.

sentences.zh: 人龍、成功等與戰，追奔三十里，至大泥峪，賊棄馬登山走。

translations.literal: Renlong, Chenggong, and the others fought them, pursued the rout thirty li to Dani Valley, and the bandits abandoned their horses and fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong, Chenggong, and the others fought them, pursued the rout thirty li to Dani Valley, and the rebels abandoned their horses and fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 七月，高迎祥、張獻忠掠秦安、清水，人龍偕全昌破之張家川。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Gao Yingxiang and Zhang Xianzhong plundered Qin’an and Qingshui; Renlong together with Quanchang defeated them at Zhangjiachuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Gao Yingxiang and Zhang Xianzhong plundered Qin’an and Qingshui; Renlong and Quanchang defeated them at Zhangjiachuan.

sentences.zh: 已而失利，都司田應龍等死。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they met defeat, and Commandant Tian Yinglong and others died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they were defeated, and commandant Tian Yinglong and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 八月，高傑降，承疇令人龍及遊擊孫守法挾之趨富平，乘夜擊敗賊。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Gao Jie surrendered; Chengchou ordered Renlong and the raider Sun Shoufa to escort him toward Fuping and strike the bandits by night, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Gao Jie surrendered; Chengchou ordered Renlong and raider Sun Shoufa to escort him toward Fuping and strike the rebels by night, defeating them.

sentences.zh: 人龍尋移守延綏。

translations.literal: Before long Renlong shifted to garrison Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Renlong was shifted to garrison Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 九年七月從巡撫孫傳庭大破賊盩啡，擒迎祥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year he followed Governor Sun Chuanting in a great defeat of bandits at Zhouzhi and captured Yingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year he followed Governor Sun Chuanting in a great victory over the rebels at Zhouzhi and the capture of Yingxiang.

sentences.zh: 九月，惠登相等屯寶雞，承疇遣人龍等往擊，戰于賈家村。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Hui Dengxiang and others were encamped at Baoji; Chengchou sent Renlong and others to strike them, and battle was joined at Jia Family Village.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Hui Dengxiang and others were encamped at Baoji; Chengchou sent Renlong and others against them, and battle was joined at Jia Family Village.

sentences.zh: 追奔，為賊所截。

translations.literal: In the pursuit he was cut off by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During the pursuit he was cut off by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 川將曾榮耀等來援，敗去，人龍坐褫官立功。

translations.literal: Sichuan generals Zeng Rongyao and others came to the rescue but were defeated and withdrew; Renlong was stripped of rank pending merit redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan generals Zeng Rongyao and others came to the rescue but were beaten back; Renlong was stripped of rank and ordered to redeem himself with merit.

sentences.zh: 十年，小紅狼圍漢中，瑞王告急。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Little Red Wolf besieged Hanzhong, and the Prince of Rui sent an urgent appeal.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Little Red Wolf besieged Hanzhong, and the Prince of Rui sent an urgent appeal for help.

sentences.zh: 承疇率人龍兵由兩當趨救，賊解去，詔復人龍官。

translations.literal: Chengchou led Renlong’s troops by way of Liangdang to the rescue; the bandits lifted the siege, and an edict restored Renlong’s rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou led Renlong’s troops by way of Liangdang to the rescue; when the rebels lifted the siege, an edict restored Renlong’s rank.

sentences.zh: 徽、秦逸賊東趨平、鳳，人龍躡至柳林，不利。

translations.literal: Straggling bandits of Hui and Qin marched east toward Ping and Feng; Renlong followed to Liulin but fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Straggling rebels from Hui and Qin marched east toward Ping and Feng; Renlong followed them to Liulin but fared poorly.

sentences.zh: 賊窺西安，人龍禦之，斬獲多。

translations.literal: The bandits probed Xi’an; Renlong blocked them and took many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels probed Xi’an, Renlong blocked them and took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 其冬，自成、登相入四川，承疇率人龍等往援。

translations.literal: That winter Zicheng and Dengxiang entered Sichuan, and Chengchou led Renlong and others to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zicheng and Dengxiang entered Sichuan, and Chengchou led Renlong and others to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 歲暮至廣元，賊已逼成都，自成別由松潘還陝右。

translations.literal: At year’s end they reached Guangyuan; the bandits had already pressed Chengdu, and Zicheng separately returned to Shaanxi by way of Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: At year’s end they reached Guangyuan; the rebels had already pressed Chengdu, while Zicheng separately returned to Shaanxi by way of Songpan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，承疇督人龍等自階、文窮追，自成走入西羌界，人龍與曹變蛟等大戰二十七日。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chengchou supervised Renlong and others in pursuit from Jie and Wen to the limit, and Zicheng fled into the Western Qiang frontier; Renlong and Cao Bianjiao and others fought great battles for twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Chengchou led Renlong and others in pursuit from Jie and Wen to the limit; Zicheng fled into the Western Qiang frontier, and Renlong, Cao Bianjiao, and others fought major engagements for twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 自成引殘卒入塞，竄山中，謀入四川，為人龍及馬科所追。

translations.literal: Zicheng led his remnant troops inside the passes and hid in the mountains, plotting to enter Sichuan, but was pursued by Renlong and Ma Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng led his remnant troops inside the passes and hid in the mountains, plotting to enter Sichuan, but Renlong and Ma Ke pursued him.

sentences.zh: 突漢中，扼于左光先。

translations.literal: He suddenly burst into Hanzhong and was blocked by Zuo Guangxian.
translations.idiomatic: He suddenly burst into Hanzhong and was blocked by Zuo Guangxian.

sentences.zh: 其党祁總管降，自成幾滅。

translations.literal: His partisan Qi Zongguan surrendered, and Zicheng was nearly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: His partisan Qi Zongguan surrendered, and Zicheng was nearly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 詳《變蛟傳》。

translations.literal: Details are in the biography of Bianjiao.
translations.idiomatic: The details are given in the biography of Cao Bianjiao.

sentences.zh: 其冬，京師戒嚴，擢人龍總兵官，帥師入衛。

translations.literal: That winter the capital was placed on alert; Renlong was promoted to regional commander and led troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the capital was placed on alert; Renlong was promoted to regional commander and led troops to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 人龍所部多降賊，至山西而噪，尋撫定。

translations.literal: Many in Renlong’s command were former surrendered bandits; reaching Shanxi they mutinied, but were soon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Renlong’s men were former surrendered rebels; in Shanxi they mutinied but were soon pacified.

sentences.zh: 抵京，與變蛟等奏捷于太平。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he and Bianjiao and others reported victory at Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he and Bianjiao and others reported victory at Taiping.

sentences.zh: 明年事定，還陝西。

translations.literal: The next year, when affairs were settled, he returned to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, once affairs were settled, he returned to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 其秋，張獻忠、羅汝才叛，謀入陝。

translations.literal: That autumn Zhang Xianzhong and Luo Rucai rebelled and plotted to enter Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhang Xianzhong and Luo Rucai rebelled and plotted to enter Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 人龍及副將李國奇等扼之興安，乃入川東。

translations.literal: Renlong and Vice General Li Guoqi blocked them at Xing’an, so they entered eastern Sichuan instead.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong and vice general Li Guoqi blocked them at Xing’an, so they turned into eastern Sichuan instead.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌檄陝西總督鄭崇儉率人龍、國奇軍會剿。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang ordered Shaanxi Governor-General Zheng Chongjian to lead Renlong’s and Guoqi’s armies in a joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang ordered Shaanxi governor-general Zheng Chongjian to lead the armies of Renlong and Guoqi in a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 十二月，人龍擊賊，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Renlong struck the bandits and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Renlong attacked the rebels and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月與左良玉大破賊瑪瑙山，人龍得一千三百餘級，降賊將二十五人。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year he and Zuo Liangyu inflicted a great defeat on bandits at Agate Mountain; Renlong took more than thirteen hundred heads and twenty-five surrendered bandit generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirteenth year he and Zuo Liangyu crushed the rebels at Agate Mountain; Renlong took more than thirteen hundred heads and accepted the surrender of twenty-five rebel generals.

sentences.zh: 六月，汝才、登相犯開縣，總兵鄭嘉棟擊之仙寺嶺，人龍擊之馬弱溪，共斬首一千二百。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Rucai and Dengxiang invaded Kaixian; Regional Commander Zheng Jiadong struck them at Xiansi Ridge and Renlong struck them at Maruo Stream, together beheading twelve hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Rucai and Dengxiang invaded Kaixian; regional commander Zheng Jiadong struck them at Xiansi Ridge and Renlong at Maruo Stream, together taking twelve hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 汝才、登相東西走，追之不能及。

translations.literal: Rucai and Dengxiang fled east and west; pursuit could not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai and Dengxiang fled east and west, and pursuit could not overtake them.

sentences.zh: 時賊盡集於川，監軍萬元吉令川將守巴、巫諸隘，人龍、國奇及楚將張應元、汪雲龍、張奏凱專主追擊。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits were all gathered in Sichuan; Supervising Army Commander Wan Yuanji ordered Sichuan generals to hold the passes at Ba and Wu and the other barriers, while Renlong, Guoqi, and the Chu generals Zhang Yingyuan, Wang Yunlong, and Zhang Zoukai were charged solely with pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebels were concentrated in Sichuan; supervising army commander Wan Yuanji ordered Sichuan troops to hold the passes at Ba, Wu, and other barriers, while Renlong, Guoqi, and the Huguang generals Zhang Yingyuan, Wang Yunlong, and Zhang Zoukai were assigned solely to pursuit.

sentences.zh: 及應元軍入夔，營土地嶺，人龍逗留不至，諸軍遂大敗，人龍竟還陝。

translations.literal: When Yingyuan’s army entered Kui and encamped at Tudi Ridge, Renlong lingered and did not arrive; the armies therefore suffered a great defeat, and Renlong in the end returned to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingyuan’s army entered Kui and encamped at Tudi Ridge, Renlong lingered and never came up; the allied armies were therefore crushed, and Renlong eventually returned to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 已而獻忠、汝才陷劍州，趨廣元，將從間道入漢中。

translations.literal: Before long Xianzhong and Rucai took Jianzhou and pressed toward Guangyuan, intending to enter Hanzhong by a bypath.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xianzhong and Rucai took Jianzhou and pressed toward Guangyuan, intending to enter Hanzhong by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 人龍拒之陽平、百丈二關，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Renlong blocked them at Yangping and Baizhang passes, and the bandits therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong blocked them at Yangping and Baizhang passes, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十二月，嗣昌至重慶，三檄人龍會師，不至。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Sichang reached Chongqing and three times ordered Renlong to join forces; he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yang Sichang arrived at Chongqing and thrice summoned He Renlong to unite their armies, but Renlong never came.

sentences.zh: 初，嗣昌惡左良玉，許人龍代為平賊將軍。

translations.literal: At first Sichang hated Zuo Liangyu and had promised Renlong that he would replace him as Pacification-General against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sichang had despised Zuo Liangyu and had promised He Renlong that he would install him as general for the pacification of the bandits in Liangyu's stead.

sentences.zh: 及戰瑪瑙山，良玉功第一，嗣昌語人龍姑待之。

translations.literal: When they fought at Mount Agate, Liangyu's achievement ranked first, and Sichang told Renlong to wait for now.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle at Mount Agate, where Liangyu won the top honors, Sichang told Renlong to bide his time.

sentences.zh: 人龍大觖望，效良玉所為，不奉約束，嗣昌亦不能制。

translations.literal: Renlong was greatly disappointed, imitated what Liangyu did, would not obey discipline, and Sichang could not control him either.
translations.idiomatic: He Renlong was bitterly disappointed. He began to act as Liangyu did—defying orders—and Sichang could no longer restrain him.

sentences.zh: 賊陷瀘州而北，人龍屯小市廂，隔一水不擊。

translations.literal: The bandits took Luzhou and marched north; Renlong camped at Xiaoshixiang, separated by one stream, and did not attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels captured Luzhou and drove north, Renlong encamped at Xiaoshixiang on the far bank of a river and refused to strike.

sentences.zh: 賊遂越成都走漢州德陽，人龍軍大噪而歸。

translations.literal: The bandits then crossed Chengdu and fled toward Hanzhou and Deyang; Renlong's army made a great clamor and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swept past Chengdu toward Hanzhou and Deyang while Renlong's troops raised a din and marched home.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，嗣昌卒，丁啟睿代，令人龍、國奇出當陽，擊敗自成於靈寶山中。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year Sichang died; Ding Qirui replaced him and ordered Renlong and Guo Qi out through Dangyang, defeating Zicheng in the mountains of Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year Sichang died. Ding Qirui took his place and sent Renlong and Guo Qi through Dangyang, where they defeated Li Zicheng in the hills of Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 人龍子大明戰歿。

translations.literal: Renlong's son Daming died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong's son Daming fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 九月，總督傅宗龍統人龍、國奇軍出關，次新蔡，遇賊孟家莊。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Grand Coordinator Fu Zonglong commanded the armies of Renlong and Guo Qi out of the pass, halted newly at Xincai, and met the bandits at Mengjiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Governor-General Fu Zonglong led the forces of Renlong and Guo Qi out through the pass and had just reached Xincai when they encountered the rebels at Mengjiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 將戰，人龍先走，國奇戰不勝，亦走，宗龍遂歿。

translations.literal: As battle was about to begin Renlong fled first; Guo Qi fought without victory and also fled, and Zonglong then died.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle Renlong ran first. Guo Qi could not hold and fled too, and Fu Zonglong perished.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，總督汪喬年出關擊賊，人龍及鄭嘉棟、牛成虎從。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year Grand Coordinator Wang Qiaonian went out of the pass to strike the bandits; Renlong, Zheng Jiadong, and Niu Chenghu followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year Governor-General Wang Qiaonian marched out to attack the rebels, with He Renlong, Zheng Jiadong, and Niu Chenghu in his train.

sentences.zh: 至襄城遇賊，復不戰走，喬年亦歿。

translations.literal: At Xiangcheng they met the bandits, again refused to fight and fled, and Qiaonian also died.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangcheng they ran into the rebels, once again declined to fight and bolted, and Wang Qiaonian likewise perished.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，欲誅之，慮其為變，姑奪職，戴罪視事。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and wished to execute them, but fearing they might revolt, temporarily stripped them of office and allowed them to serve while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and meant to put them to death, but fearing mutiny he merely stripped their ranks for the moment and ordered them to continue on duty while awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 及孫傳庭督師陝西，帝授以意。

translations.literal: When Sun Chuanting supervised the army in Shaanxi, the emperor imparted his intent to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Chuanting took command in Shaanxi, the emperor confided his wishes to him.

sentences.zh: 人龍駐咸陽虞禍，曉夜為備。

translations.literal: Renlong was stationed at Yuta, Xianyang, and made preparations day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong was posted at Yuta near Xianyang and kept his men on alert around the clock.

sentences.zh: 傳庭以人龍家米脂，其宗族多在賊中，未可輕發，在道佯上疏曰：「人龍臣舊將，願貰其罪，俾從臣自效。

translations.literal: Chuanting, because Renlong's family was from Mizhi and many of his clan were among the bandits, did not dare act lightly; on the road he feigned a memorial saying: "Renlong is my former officer; I beg to spare his crime and let him serve me to prove himself."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuanting knew Renlong came from Mizhi and that much of his clan still rode with the rebels, so he dared not move too soon. While still on the road he filed a feigned memorial: "He Renlong is a veteran under my command. I beg leave to redeem his offense and let him follow me and prove his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」帝亦佯許之。

translations.literal: The emperor also feigned approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pretended to consent.

sentences.zh: 人龍稍自安。

translations.literal: Renlong gradually felt reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong's fears eased a little.

sentences.zh: 傳庭至陝，密與巡撫張爾忠謀，以五月朔召人龍計事，數其罪斬之。

translations.literal: Chuanting reached Shaanxi, secretly plotted with Grand Secretary Zhang Erzhong, and on the first day of the fifth month summoned Renlong to discuss affairs, enumerated his crimes, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Chuanting reached Shaanxi he plotted in secret with the provincial governor Zhang Erzhong. On the first day of the fifth month he summoned Renlong to a council, recited his crimes, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 其部將周國卿將精卒二百人與同黨魏大亨、賀國賢、高進庫等將逃還涇陽取其孥，與賊為亂。

translations.literal: His subordinate commander Zhou Guoqing with two hundred crack troops and fellow conspirators Wei Datong, He Guoxian, Gao Jinku, and others planned to flee back to Jingyang to seize their families and join the bandits in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Among his officers, Zhou Guoqing gathered two hundred picked men and, with accomplices Wei Datong, He Guoxian, Gao Jinku, and others, planned to flee to Jingyang, seize their families, and raise rebellion with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 爾忠遣參將孫守法先入涇陽，質其妻子。

translations.literal: Erzhong sent Assistant-General Sun Shoufa ahead into Jingyang to take their wives and children hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhong sent Assistant Commander Sun Shoufa ahead into Jingyang to hold their wives and children as hostages.

sentences.zh: 國卿窮，謀斬大亨等以降。

translations.literal: Guoqing was cornered and plotted to kill Datong and the others to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Boxed in, Guoqing planned to kill Datong and the rest to win surrender.

sentences.zh: 爾忠密聞之大亨，遂斬國卿，函送其首。

translations.literal: Erzhong secretly informed Datong, who then beheaded Guoqing and sent his head in a box.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhong secretly tipped Datong off, who then killed Guoqing and sent his head in a casket.

sentences.zh: 他部將高傑、高汝利、賀勇、董學禮等十四人俱仍故官，一軍乃定。

translations.literal: The other subordinates Gao Jie, Gao Ruli, He Yong, Dong Xueli, and fourteen others all kept their former posts, and the army was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The other officers—Gao Jie, Gao Ruli, He Yong, Dong Xueli, and fourteen besides—all kept their former ranks, and the army was steadied at last.

sentences.zh: 高傑，米脂人。

translations.literal: Gao Jie was a native of Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie was a native of Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 與李自成同邑，同起為盜。

translations.literal: He and Li Zicheng were from the same district; they rose together as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Zicheng were from the same district and had risen together as bandits.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年閏八月，總督陳奇瑜遣參將賀人龍救隴州，被圍大困。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month of the seventh year of Chongzhen, Grand Coordinator Chen Qiyu sent Assistant-General He Renlong to relieve Longzhou; he was besieged and in great straits.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month of the seventh year of Chongzhen, Governor-General Chen Qiyu sent Assistant Commander He Renlong to relieve Longzhou, where he was besieged and hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 自成令傑遺書約人龍反，不報。

translations.literal: Zicheng ordered Jie to send a letter inviting Renlong to defect; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng ordered Jie to send a letter inviting Renlong to defect, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 使者歸，先見傑，後見自成。

translations.literal: The messenger returned, saw Jie first and Zicheng afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger returned and was received by Jie before he saw Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 比圍城兩月不拔，自成心疑傑，遣別部將往代，傑歸守營。

translations.literal: When after two months the siege could not be raised, Zicheng grew suspicious of Jie and sent another commander to replace him; Jie returned to guard the camp.
translations.idiomatic: After two months the siege still held, Zicheng grew suspicious of Jie and sent another commander to take his place, and Jie returned to guard the camp.

sentences.zh: 自成妻邢氏武多智，掌軍資，每日支糧仗。

translations.literal: Zicheng's wife Lady Xing was martial and very shrewd; she controlled military supplies and issued rations and arms daily.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng's wife, Lady Xing, was fierce and clever; she managed the army stores and issued grain and weapons every day.

sentences.zh: 傑過氏營，分合符驗。

translations.literal: When Jie passed Lady Xing's camp they compared tally tokens.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie passed through Lady Xing's camp they matched their tally tokens.

sentences.zh: 氏偉傑貌，與之通，恐自成覺，謀歸降。

translations.literal: The Lady admired Jie's looks, took him as lover, feared Zicheng would discover it, and plotted to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xing was struck by Jie's appearance, took him as her lover, and fearing Zicheng would find out, plotted to defect.

sentences.zh: 次年八月遂竊邢氏來歸。

translations.literal: The next year in the eighth month he stole Lady Xing away and came over to the government side.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the eighth month, he slipped away with Lady Xing and surrendered to the government.

sentences.zh: 洪承疇以付人龍，使其遊擊孫守法挾以破賊，取立效為信，自是傑常隸人龍麾下。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou handed him to Renlong and had mobile-guard Sun Shoufa use him to break the bandits, requiring immediate proof of merit; from then on Jie usually served under Renlong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou placed him under Renlong and had the mobile brigadier Sun Shoufa use him against the rebels, demanding proof of merit at once; thereafter Jie usually served under Renlong.

sentences.zh: 十三年，張獻忠敗於瑪瑙山，竄興、歸界上，傑隨人龍及副將李國奇大敗之鹽井。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhang Xianzhong was defeated at Mount Agate and fled along the Xing and Gui border; Jie followed Renlong and Vice Commander Li Guoqi to crush him badly at Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhang Xianzhong was beaten at Mount Agate and fled along the Xing–Gui frontier; Jie followed Renlong and Vice Commander Li Guoqi to rout him at Salt Wells.

sentences.zh: 十五年，人龍以罪誅，命傑為實授遊擊。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Renlong was executed for his crimes and Jie was appointed substantive mobile brigadier.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Renlong was executed for his crimes, and Jie was given a substantive appointment as mobile brigadier.

sentences.zh: 十月，陝西總督孫傳庭至南陽，自成與羅汝才西行逆之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Shaanxi governor Sun Chuanting reached Nanyang; Zicheng and Luo Rucai marched west to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Shaanxi governor Sun Chuanting reached Nanyang; Li Zicheng and Luo Rucai marched west to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 傳庭以傑與魯某為先鋒，遇于塚頭，大戰敗賊，追奔六十里。

translations.literal: Chuanting made Jie and a certain Lu his vanguard; they met at Zhongtou, heavily defeated the bandits, and pursued them sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting made Jie and a certain Lu his vanguard; at Zhongtou they fought a great battle, routed the rebels, and pursued them sixty li.

sentences.zh: 汝才見自成敗來救，繞出官軍後。

translations.literal: Rucai, seeing Zicheng defeated, came to the rescue and swung around behind the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zicheng beaten, Rucai came to his aid and circled behind the government forces.

sentences.zh: 後軍左勷望見賊，怖而先奔，眾軍皆奔，遂大潰，傑所亡失獨少。

translations.literal: Rear-guard commander Zuo Liang saw the bandits, was frightened and fled first; all the armies fled and there was a great rout, yet Jie's losses alone were few.
translations.idiomatic: The rear-guard commander Zuo Liang caught sight of the rebels, panicked, and fled first; the whole army broke and fled in a rout, yet Jie alone suffered few losses.

sentences.zh: 十六年進副總兵，與總兵白廣恩為軍鋒，兩人皆降將也。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted deputy commander-in-chief; he and full commander Bai Guang'en were army vanguard—both were surrendered bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted deputy commander-in-chief; he and the full commander Bai Guang'en served as the army's spearhead—both were former rebels who had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 廣恩鷙鰲，素不奉約束，而傑尤兇暴。

translations.literal: Guang'en was fierce and obstinate and never obeyed discipline, while Jie was especially brutal.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'en was savage and headstrong and had never submitted to discipline; Jie was even more violent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以傑為自成所切齒，故命隸傳庭辦賊。

translations.literal: The court, because Jie was bitterly hated by Zicheng, ordered him to serve under Chuanting against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Zicheng hated Jie with a personal fury, the court assigned him to Chuanting's command to hunt the rebels.

sentences.zh: 九月從傳庭克寶豐，復郟縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he followed Chuanting in taking Baofeng and recovering Jiaxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he followed Chuanting in capturing Baofeng and recovering Jiaxian.

sentences.zh: 時官軍乘勝深入，乏食。

translations.literal: At the time the government army, pressing its victory in a deep advance, lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: The government army, drunk on victory, had pushed deep into enemy country and was starving.

sentences.zh: 降將李際遇通賊，自成帥精騎大至。

translations.literal: The surrendered general Li Jiyu colluded with the bandits, and Zicheng came at the head of crack cavalry in strength.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered general Li Jiyu was in league with the rebels, and Li Zicheng arrived at the head of a great force of elite cavalry.

sentences.zh: 傳庭問計于諸將，傑請戰，廣恩不可。

translations.literal: Chuanting asked the commanders' counsel; Jie urged battle, Guang'en refused.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting asked his generals for counsel; Jie urged an attack, Guang'en refused.

sentences.zh: 傳庭以廣恩為怯，廣恩不懌，引所部遁去。

translations.literal: Chuanting took Guang'en for a coward; Guang'en was displeased and led his own troops away in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting judged Guang'en a coward; stung, Guang'en led his own troops away.

sentences.zh: 官軍接戰，陷伏中。

translations.literal: The government army joined battle and fell into an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: The government army engaged and walked into an ambush.

sentences.zh: 傑登嶺上望之曰：「不可支矣。

translations.literal: Jie climbed a ridge, looked on, and said: "It cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: Jie climbed a hill to watch and said, "This cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 」亦麾眾退。

translations.literal: He also waved his troops to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He too ordered his men to fall back.

sentences.zh: 軍遂大奔，死者數萬。

translations.literal: The army then fled in a great rush; tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: The army broke and ran; tens of thousands were killed.

sentences.zh: 廣恩走汝州不救，傑乃隨傳庭走河北。

translations.literal: Guang'en fled to Ruzhou without aiding them; Jie then followed Chuanting in flight to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'en fled to Ruzhou without lending aid; Jie followed Chuanting in flight into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 已而自山西渡河，轉入潼關，廣恩已先至。

translations.literal: Afterward they crossed the river from Shanxi on their own, turned into Tong Pass, and Guang'en had already arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: Later they crossed the Yellow River from Shanxi, swung back toward Tong Pass, and found Guang'en already there ahead of them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，自成攻關，廣恩力戰。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zicheng attacked the pass; Guang'en fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Li Zicheng assaulted the pass, and Guang'en fought hard.

sentences.zh: 而傑怨廣恩以寶豐之敗不救己，亦擁眾不肯救。

translations.literal: But Jie resented Guang'en for not rescuing him at the Baofeng defeat and also held his forces back and refused to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, still bitter that Guang'en had not rescued him at Baofeng, likewise held his troops back and refused to help.

sentences.zh: 廣恩戰敗，關遂破，傳庭被殺。

translations.literal: Guang'en was defeated in battle, the pass was then broken, and Chuanting was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'en was beaten, the pass fell, and Chuanting was killed.

sentences.zh: 自成破西安，據之。

translations.literal: Zicheng broke Xi'an and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng took Xi'an and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 傑北走延安，賊將李過追傑。

translations.literal: Jie fled north to Yan'an; the bandit commander Li Guo pursued Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Jie fled north to Yan'an, pursued by the rebel commander Li Guo.

sentences.zh: 傑東走宜川，河冰適合，遂渡，入蒲津以守。

translations.literal: Jie fled east to Yichuan; the river ice happened to be solid enough to cross, so he crossed and entered Pujin to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Jie turned east to Yichuan; the river ice was firm enough to bear him, so he crossed and took post at Pujin.

sentences.zh: 賊至，冰解不得渡，乃免。

translations.literal: The bandits arrived; the ice broke up and they could not cross, and so he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came up, the ice had broken and they could not follow; he was spared.

sentences.zh: 廣恩既敗，走固原，為賊將追及，遂以城降。

translations.literal: Guang'en, already defeated, fled to Guyuan, was overtaken by a bandit commander, and then surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'en, already beaten, fled to Guyuan, was overtaken by a rebel commander, and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 十七年進傑總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jie was promoted full commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Jie was promoted to full commander.

sentences.zh: 帝令總督李化熙率傑兵馳救山西，而蒲州、平陽已陷久，傑退至澤州，沿途大掠，賊遂薄太原。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Grand Coordinator Li Huaxi to lead Jie's troops in a rush to relieve Shanxi; but Puzhou and Pingyang had long fallen, Jie retreated to Zezhou, plundered heavily along the way, and the bandits then pressed on Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Governor-General Li Huaxi to rush Jie's troops to relieve Shanxi, but Puzhou and Pingyang had been lost for some time. Jie fell back to Zezhou, plundering savagely as he went, and the rebels closed on Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，傑南走，福王封傑興平伯，列于四鎮，領揚州，駐城外。

translations.literal: When the capital fell Jie fled south; the Prince of Fu enfeoffed Jie as Marquis of Xingping, ranked him among the Four Garrisons, put him in charge of Yangzhou, and he camped outside the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Jie fled south. The Prince of Fu enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xingping, ranked him among the Four Garrisons, gave him Yangzhou to hold, and he encamped outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 傑固欲入城，揚州民畏傑不納。

translations.literal: Jie insisted on entering the city; the people of Yangzhou feared Jie and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was determined to enter the city, but the people of Yangzhou, terrified of him, refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 傑攻城急，日掠廂村婦女，民益惡之。

translations.literal: Jie pressed the siege fiercely, day by day plundering women from the suburbs and villages, and the people hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Jie pressed the siege hard and day after day seized women from the suburbs and villages; the populace loathed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 知府馬鳴騄、推官湯來賀堅守月餘。

translations.literal: Prefect Ma Mingcong and Assistant Magistrate Tang Laihe held firm for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Ma Mingcong and Assistant Magistrate Tang Laihe held out for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 傑知不可攻，意稍怠。

translations.literal: Jie knew the city could not be taken and his ardor slackened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city could not be taken, Jie's zeal for the assault cooled.

sentences.zh: 閣部史可法議以瓜州予傑，乃止。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shi Kefa proposed giving Guazhou to Jie, and it then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shi Kefa proposed granting him Guazhou instead, and the siege was called off.

sentences.zh: 九月命傑移駐徐州，以左中允衛胤文兼兵科給事中監其軍西討。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jie was ordered to relocate his camp to Xuzhou, with Left Attendant Instructor Wei Yinwen also serving as supervising censor of the Bureau of Military Affairs over his army for a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jie was ordered to move his camp to Xuzhou, with Left Attendant Instructor Wei Yinwen appointed supervising censor of military affairs to oversee his army on a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 徐州土賊程繼孔被擒至京師，乘李自成亂逃歸，十二月，傑擒斬之。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou local bandit Cheng Jikong had been captured and taken to the capital; he escaped home amid Li Zicheng's turmoil. In the twelfth month Jie captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuzhou bandit Cheng Jikong had once been captured and sent to the capital, but escaped home during Li Zicheng's upheaval; in the twelfth month Jie seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 加太子少傅，廕一子，世襲錦衣僉事。

translations.literal: He was promoted Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, one son was granted privilege, and hereditary appointment as Assistant Commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; one son received an imperial grace, with hereditary rank as assistant commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，傑伏兵要擊黃得功於土橋，得功幾不免，兩鎮遂相仇怨，事見《得功傳》。

translations.literal: Earlier Jie had lain in ambush to attack Huang Degong at Tuqiao; Degong nearly perished, and the two garrisons bore mutual enmity—the affair is recorded in the Biography of Degong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jie had set an ambush for Huang Degong at Tuqiao and nearly killed him; the two garrisons became bitter enemies, as told in the Biography of Degong.

sentences.zh: 傑爭揚州時，可法頗為所窘。

translations.literal: When Jie struggled for Yangzhou, Kefa was quite pressed by him.
translations.idiomatic: During Jie's struggle for Yangzhou, Kefa had been sorely pressed by him.

sentences.zh: 至是，傑感可法忠，與謀恢復。

translations.literal: By this time Jie was moved by Kefa's loyalty and joined him in planning recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jie was moved by Kefa's loyalty and joined him in planning the reconquest.

sentences.zh: 議調得功與劉澤清二鎮赴邳、宿防河，傑自提兵直趨歸、開，且瞰宛、洛、荊、襄，以為根本。

translations.literal: They planned to move Degong's and Liu Zeqing's two garrisons to Pi and Su to guard the river, while Jie himself would lead troops straight toward Guide and Kaifeng and moreover command Nanyang, Luoyang, Jingzhou, and Xiangyang as his base.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed shifting the garrisons of Degong and Liu Zeqing to Pi and Su to hold the river line, while Jie himself would lead troops straight for Guide and Kaifeng and keep an eye on Nanyang, Luoyang, Jingzhou, and Xiangyang as his strategic base.

sentences.zh: 遂具疏上之，語激切。

translations.literal: He then drew up a memorial and submitted it; the language was urgent and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up a memorial and submitted it in language fierce and impassioned.

sentences.zh: 且云：「得功與臣猶介介前事。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "Degong and I still harbor past grievances."
translations.idiomatic: In it he wrote: "Degong and I still nurse old grudges."

sentences.zh: 臣知報君雪恥而已，安能與同列較短長哉！

translations.literal: "I know only to repay the sovereign and wash away shame—how could I measure myself against my peers!"
translations.idiomatic: "I care only to repay my sovereign and avenge our shame—how could I bicker over rank with my fellows!"

sentences.zh: 」然得功終不欲為傑後勁，而澤清尤狡橫難任。

translations.literal: Yet Degong in the end was unwilling to serve as Jie's rear support, and Zeqing was especially cunning, arrogant, and hard to employ.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Degong would not serve as his rearguard, and Zeqing was especially sly, overbearing, and impossible to command.

sentences.zh: 可法不得已，調劉良佐赴徐與傑為聲援。

translations.literal: Kefa had no choice but to transfer Liu Liangzuo to Xuzhou to give Jie vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: Kefa had no choice but to transfer Liu Liangzuo to Xuzhou to back Jie up.

sentences.zh: 順治二年正月，傑抵歸德。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Shunzhi Jie reached Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Shunzhi, Jie reached Guide.

sentences.zh: 總兵許定國方駐睢州，有言其送子渡河者。

translations.literal: Full commander Xu Dingguo was then stationed at Suizhou; there was talk that he had sent his son across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The commander Xu Dingguo was then posted at Suizhou, and word spread that he had sent his son across the river to safety.

sentences.zh: 傑招定國來會，不應。

translations.literal: Jie summoned Dingguo to a meeting; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Jie summoned Dingguo to a parley; he did not come.

sentences.zh: 復邀巡撫越其傑、巡按陳潛夫同往睢州，定國始郊逆。

translations.literal: Again he invited Grand Coordinator Yue Qijie and Investigating Censor Chen Qianfu to go with him to Suizhou; only then did Dingguo come out to the suburbs to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie then asked the governor Yue Qijie and the investigating censor Chen Qianfu to accompany him to Suizhou; only then did Dingguo come out to the suburbs to receive them.

sentences.zh: 其傑諷傑勿入城，傑心輕定國，不聽，遂入城。

translations.literal: Qijie urged Jie not to enter the city; Jie thought lightly of Dingguo, did not listen, and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qijie warned Jie not to enter the city, but Jie despised Dingguo, ignored the advice, and went in.

sentences.zh: 十一日，定國置酒享傑。

translations.literal: On the eleventh Dingguo set out wine to entertain Jie.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh, Dingguo laid on a feast for Jie.

sentences.zh: 傑飲酣，為定國刻行期，且微及送子事。

translations.literal: Jie drank deep, fixed a marching date for Dingguo, and lightly touched on the matter of sending his son away.
translations.idiomatic: Jie drank heavily, pressed a departure date on Dingguo, and obliquely raised the story of his son's flight.

sentences.zh: 定國益疑，無離睢意。

translations.literal: Dingguo's suspicions grew; he had no intention of leaving Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo's suspicions deepened, and he had no mind to leave Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 傑固促之行，定國怒，夜伏兵傳砲大呼。

translations.literal: Jie firmly pressed him to march; Dingguo was enraged, hid troops by night, passed cannon along the line and shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Jie kept pressing him to march; enraged, Dingguo hid troops by night, passed the word along the guns, and raised a great shout.

sentences.zh: 其傑等急遁走，傑醉臥帳中未起，眾擁至定國所殺之。

translations.literal: Qijie and the others fled in haste; Jie, drunk, lay in his tent and had not risen—the crowd rushed in and killed him at Dingguo's place.
translations.idiomatic: Qijie and the others fled for their lives; Jie, drunk and still in his bed, was overrun and killed in Dingguo's quarters.

sentences.zh: 先是，傑以定國將去睢，盡發兵戍開封，所留親卒數十人而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Jie thought Dingguo would leave Suizhou, he sent out all his troops to garrison Kaifeng; only a few dozen personal guards remained.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, believing Dingguo would quit Suizhou, Jie had sent nearly all his troops to garrison Kaifeng, leaving only a few dozen of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 定國偽恭順，多選妓侍傑，而以二妓偶一卒寢。

translations.literal: Dingguo feigned deference, selected many courtesans to attend Jie, and paired two courtesans with one soldier for sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo played the obedient host, sent many courtesans to wait on Jie, and assigned two women to each soldier for the night.

sentences.zh: 卒盡醉，及聞砲欲起，為二妓所掣不得脫，皆死。

translations.literal: The soldiers all grew drunk; when they heard the cannon and wished to rise, the two courtesans held them back so they could not escape, and all died.
translations.idiomatic: The men drank themselves senseless; when the guns sounded and they tried to rise, the women held them fast so they could not escape, and every one was killed.

sentences.zh: 明日，傑部下至，攻城，老弱無孑遺。

translations.literal: The next day Jie's troops arrived, attacked the city, and not one old or young was left alive.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jie's troops came up, stormed the city, and spared neither old nor young.

sentences.zh: 定國走降大清軍。

translations.literal: Dingguo fled and surrendered to the Great Qing army.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo fled and surrendered to the Qing armies.

sentences.zh: 傑為人淫毒，揚民聞其死，皆相賀。

translations.literal: Jie as a man was lecherous and cruel; when the people of Yangzhou heard of his death they all congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was a man of violent lust and cruelty; when the people of Yangzhou heard he was dead, they celebrated in the streets.

sentences.zh: 然是行也，進取意甚銳，故時有惜之者。

translations.literal: Yet on this expedition his intent to advance was very keen, and so some at the time regretted his end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on this campaign his hunger to advance had been fierce, and some at the time mourned what he might have done.

sentences.zh: 始朝廷許諸鎮與聞國是，故傑屢條奏救降賊者，及請釋武愫於獄，不允。
