translations.literal: At the beginning the court had permitted the frontier garrisons to take part in deliberating state affairs; therefore Jie repeatedly memorialized in separate items to spare those who had surrendered from the bandits, and to request release of Wu Su from prison—the court did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first allowed the regional commanders a voice in state affairs, Jie repeatedly petitioned to spare surrendered rebels and to free Wu Su from prison; both were refused.

sentences.zh: 復疏薦吳甡、鄭三俊、金光辰、姜埰、熊開元、金聲、沈正宗等。

translations.literal: He again memorialized recommending Wu Shen, Zheng Sanjun, Jin Guangchen, Jiang Cai, Xiong Kaiyuan, Jin Sheng, Shen Zhengzong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted recommendations for Wu Shen, Zheng Sanjun, Jin Guangchen, Jiang Cai, Xiong Kaiyuan, Jin Sheng, Shen Zhengzong, and others.

sentences.zh: 大抵其時武臣風尚多類此。

translations.literal: For the most part the fashion among military officers at that time was largely of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part, the temper of military men in those days ran much the same way.

sentences.zh: 傑死，贈太子太保，以其子元爵襲興平伯。

translations.literal: When Jie died, he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; his son Yuanjue inherited the title Earl of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: After Jie's death the court posthumously named him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his son Yuanjue inherited the earldom of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 劉澤清，曹縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Zeqing was a native of Cao County.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zeqing was a native of Cao County.

sentences.zh: 以將材授遼東甯、前衛守備，遷山東都司僉書，加參將。

translations.literal: For military talent he was appointed defender of the Liaodong Ning Front Guard; he was transferred to assistant commissioner of the Shandong regional military commission with the added rank of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for martial ability, he was made defender of the Liaodong Ning Front Guard, then transferred to assistant commissioner of the Shandong command with the added rank of vice commander.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，大清兵攻鐵廠，欲據以絕豐潤糧道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen the Great Qing army attacked Tiechang, intending to seize it and cut the Fengrun grain route.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen the Qing army attacked Tiechang, aiming to hold it and sever Fengrun's grain lifeline.

sentences.zh: 援守三屯總兵楊肇基遣澤清來援，未至鐵廠一十五里，遇大兵，力戰，自辰至午不決。

translations.literal: Yang Zhaoqi, regional commander of Santun who had come to relieve the siege, sent Zeqing to aid; fifteen li short of Tiechang he met the main Qing force and fought fiercely from the chen hour to noon without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Relief commander Yang Zhaoqi of Santun sent Zeqing forward; fifteen li from Tiechang he met the main Qing force and fought from morning until noon without breaking the stalemate.

sentences.zh: 得濟師，轉戰至遵化，夾擊，遂得入城。

translations.literal: Once reinforcements arrived, he fought his way to Zunhua; pincer attacks allowed him to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements arrived, he fought through to Zunhua, and a converging attack let him enter the city.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加二級至副總兵。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was promoted two grades to vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His service was entered on the rolls of merit and he was raised two grades to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 五年以侵克軍糧被劾，詔立功沖要地。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was impeached for encroaching on and embezzling army grain; an edict ordered him to earn merit at a strategic post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was impeached for seizing and embezzling army grain; the court ordered him to redeem himself with merit at a vital post.

sentences.zh: 六年遷總兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made regional commander.

sentences.zh: 其冬加左都督，恢復登州有功。

translations.literal: That winter he was made Left Censor-in-chief for merit in recovering Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was named Left Censor-in-chief for recovering Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年詔統山東兵防漕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict put him in command of Shandong troops to guard the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict placed Shandong's troops under him to guard the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 九年，京師戒嚴，統兵入衛，令駐新城為南北控扼，復命留守通州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, with the capital under martial alert, he led troops in to guard the capital, ordered to garrison at New City to control north and south, and again ordered to remain and defend Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the capital went on war footing, he marched in with his army, was posted at New City to choke north–south traffic, and was then ordered to hold Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 加左都督、太子太師。

translations.literal: He was made Left Censor-in-chief and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He received the titles Left Censor-in-chief and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，山東大饑，民相聚為寇，曹、濮尤甚。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year Shandong suffered great famine; the people gathered as bandits, worst in Cao and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year Shandong was stricken with famine; people banded together as marauders, above all in Cao and Pu.

sentences.zh: 帝命澤清會總兵楊禦蕃兵剿捕之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zeqing to join regional commander Yang Yufan's troops in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zeqing to join regional commander Yang Yufan in hunting them down.

sentences.zh: 八月降右都督，鎮守山東防海。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was demoted to Right Censor-in-chief and charged with guarding Shandong's coast defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was reduced to Right Censor-in-chief and assigned to guard Shandong's coast.

sentences.zh: 澤清以生長山東，久鎮東省非宜，請辭任。

translations.literal: Zeqing, having grown up in Shandong, said long command of the eastern province was unsuitable and asked to resign the post.
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing, a Shandong native, argued that holding his home province for long was improper and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 帝令整旅渡河，合諸鎮星馳援剿。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to marshal his brigade, cross the river, unite with the various garrisons, and hurry to aid in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to take his brigade across the river, join the other garrisons, and race to the relief campaign.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月，賊圍開封久，澤清赴援。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year the bandits had long besieged Kaifeng; Zeqing went to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixteenth year rebels had long held Kaifeng under siege; Zeqing marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 以硃家寨去汴八里，提五千人南渡，倚河為寨，疏水環之，欲以次結八寨達大堤，築甬道，饋饟城中。

translations.literal: Because Zhujia Stockade was eight li from Bian, he led five thousand men south across the river, leaned on the river to build a camp, ringed it with ditched water, intending in sequence to link eight stockades to the great dike, build a gallery road, and supply grain into the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhujia Stockade, eight li from Bian, he ferried five thousand men south, pitched camp on the riverbank, and ringed it with channels—planning to chain eight camps to the great dike, build a covered supply road, and feed the city.

sentences.zh: 壁壘未成，賊來爭。

translations.literal: Before the ramparts were finished the bandits came to contest them.
translations.idiomatic: Before the works were finished the rebels came to dispute the ground.

sentences.zh: 相持三日，互有殺傷。

translations.literal: They contended three days with mutual casualties.
translations.idiomatic: For three days they grappled, each side taking losses.

sentences.zh: 澤清即命拔營去，惶擾奔迸，士爭舟，多溺死者。

translations.literal: Zeqing then ordered the camp struck and withdrew; panic and flight prevailed; soldiers scrambled for boats and many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing then ordered the camp broken; panic spread, men stampeded for the boats, and many drowned.

sentences.zh: 澤清為人性恇怯，懷私觀望。

translations.literal: Zeqing by nature was timid and craven, harboring private designs and watching from the sidelines.
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing was timid by nature, nursed private schemes, and hung back.

sentences.zh: 嘗妄報大捷邀賞賜，又詭稱墮馬被傷，詔賚藥資四十兩。

translations.literal: He once falsely reported a great victory to solicit rewards, and also falsely claimed he had fallen from a horse and been wounded—the court bestowed medicine money of forty taels.
translations.idiomatic: He once invented a great victory to claim reward, and another time pretended a fall from his horse had wounded him—the court sent forty taels for medicine.

sentences.zh: 命赴保定剿賊，不從，日大掠臨清。

translations.literal: Ordered to proceed to Baoding to suppress bandits, he did not obey and daily plundered greatly at Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Baoding to fight rebels, he refused and spent his days plundering Linqing.

sentences.zh: 率兵南下，所至焚劫一空。

translations.literal: Leading troops south, wherever he passed he burned and stripped all bare.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south with his army and left every place he touched burned bare.

sentences.zh: 寇氛日急，給事中韓如愈、馬嘉植皆謀奉使南歸。

translations.literal: As the marauding threat grew daily urgent, supervising secretaries Han Ruyu and Ma Jiazhi both plotted to obtain missions south to return home.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis deepened, supervising secretaries Han Ruyu and Ma Jiazhi both schemed for commissions that would take them south and home.

sentences.zh: 如愈常劾澤清，過東昌，澤清遣人殺之於道，無敢上聞者。

translations.literal: Ruyu had often impeached Zeqing; passing Dongchang, Zeqing sent men to kill him on the road, and none dared report it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu had often impeached him; when he passed Dongchang, Zeqing had him killed on the road, and no one dared report it.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，澤清走南都，福王以為諸鎮之一，封東平伯，駐廬州。

translations.literal: When the capital fell Zeqing fled to the Southern Capital; the Prince of Fu counted him among the frontier garrisons, enfeoffed him as Earl of Dongping, and stationed him at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Beijing fell, Zeqing fled to Nanjing; the Hongguang court counted him among the regional commanders, made him Earl of Dongping, and posted him at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 時武臣各占分地，賦入不以上供，恣其所用，置封疆兵事一切不問。

translations.literal: At that time each military commander occupied a separate territory; revenues were not sent up but spent as they pleased, and frontier defense they set aside entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Each commander then held his own territory, kept the taxes for himself, and ignored the defense of the realm.

sentences.zh: 與廷臣互分黨援，干預朝政，排擠異已，奏牘紛如，紀綱盡裂，而澤清所言尤狂悖。

translations.literal: With court ministers they divided into partisan camps, meddled in court politics, squeezed out dissenters—memorials piled up like snow, discipline was utterly shattered—and Zeqing's words were especially wild and reckless.
translations.idiomatic: They courted factions among the ministers, meddled in policy, and drove out rivals; memorials snowed in and discipline collapsed—and Zeqing's were the most outrageous of all.

sentences.zh: 王初立，即援靖康故事，請以今歲五月改元，又請宥故輔周延儒助餉髒銀。

translations.literal: When the king had just been enthroned, citing the Jingkang precedent he requested the reign era be changed that fifth month, and also requested pardon for former grand secretary Zhou Yanru and his tainted silver used to aid supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly enthroned, he cited the Jingkang precedent to demand a new reign title that fifth month, and asked pardon for the former grand secretary Zhou Yanru together with his tainted silver paid as war funds.

sentences.zh: 都御史劉宗周劾諸將跋扈狀，澤清遂兩疏劾宗周，且曰：「上若誅宗周，臣即卸職。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Liu Zongzhou impeached the generals' arrogant conduct; Zeqing then sent two memorials impeaching Zongzhou, saying: "If Your Majesty executes Zongzhou, your servant will resign office.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Liu Zongzhou impeached the generals for insolence; Zeqing answered with two memorials attacking Zongzhou, declaring: "If Your Majesty puts Zongzhou to death, this servant will lay down his command.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷不得已，溫詔解之。

translations.literal: " The court had no choice but to issue a mild edict to smooth the matter over.
translations.idiomatic: " The court could only soothe both sides with a gentle edict.

sentences.zh: 又請禁巡按不得拿訪追髒，請法司嚴緝故總督侯恂及其子方域，朝廷皆曲意從之。

translations.literal: He also requested that touring censors be forbidden to investigate and pursue tainted goods, and requested the judicial offices strictly arrest former governor-general Hou Xun and his son Fangyu—the court yielded to all in each case.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded that touring censors be barred from seizing illicit funds, and pressed the judiciary to hunt down the former governor-general Hou Xun and his son Fangyu—the court bent to every request.

sentences.zh: 順治二年四月，揚州告急，命澤清等往援，而澤清已潛謀輸款矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Shunzhi Yangzhou was in urgent alarm; Zeqing and others were ordered to aid, but Zeqing had already secretly planned to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi year two Yangzhou was in peril; Zeqing was ordered to the rescue, but he had already secretly opened surrender talks.

sentences.zh: 大清惡其反覆，磔誅之。

translations.literal: The Great Qing, hating his treachery, executed him by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing, despising his double-dealing, had him torn apart in execution.

sentences.zh: 澤清頗涉文藝，好吟詠。

translations.literal: Zeqing was somewhat versed in letters and fond of composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing dabbled in letters and loved to versify.

sentences.zh: 嘗召客飲酒唱和。

translations.literal: He would summon guests to drink wine and sing in alternation.
translations.idiomatic: He often gathered guests for wine and exchanged lines of poetry.

sentences.zh: 幕中蓄兩猿，以名呼之即至。

translations.literal: In his staff he kept two gibbons that came when called by name.
translations.idiomatic: His staff kept two gibbons trained to come at the call of their names.

sentences.zh: 一日，宴其故人子，酌酒金甌中，甌可容三升許，呼猿捧酒跪送客。

translations.literal: One day entertaining his old friend's son, he poured wine into a golden bowl; the bowl could hold about three sheng; he called the gibbon to hold the wine kneeling to serve the guest.
translations.idiomatic: One day he entertained an old friend's son, poured wine into a golden bowl that held some three sheng, and had a gibbon kneel and present it to the guest.

sentences.zh: 猿猙獰甚，客戰掉，逡巡不敢取。

translations.literal: The gibbon was very fierce in aspect; the guest trembled in fear and hesitated, not daring to take it.
translations.idiomatic: The beast looked savage; the guest shook with fear and hung back, afraid to take the cup.

sentences.zh: 澤清笑曰：「君怖耶？

translations.literal: Zeqing laughed: "Are you afraid?
translations.idiomatic: Zeqing laughed: "Are you frightened?

sentences.zh: 」命取囚撲死階下，剜其腦及心肝，置甌中，和酒，付猿捧之前。

translations.literal: " He ordered a prisoner taken and beaten to death on the steps, his brain and heart and liver scooped out, placed in the bowl, mixed with wine, and handed to the gibbon to hold before the guest.
translations.idiomatic: " He had a prisoner dragged out and clubbed to death on the steps, his brains and heart and liver scooped into the bowl, stirred into the wine, and set before the guest again in the gibbon's paws.

sentences.zh: 飲酹，顏色自若。

translations.literal: He drank a libation, his countenance calm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: He drank his toast, face unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其凶忍多此類。

translations.literal: His ferocity and cruelty were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His cruelty ran to such things again and again.

sentences.zh: 祖寬，遼東人。

translations.literal: Zu Kuan was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Kuan came from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 少有勇力。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was strong and bold.

sentences.zh: 給侍祖大壽家，從軍有功，累官寧遠參將。

translations.literal: He served in Zu Dashou's household; following the army he had merit, and rose by accumulated posts to vice commander of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Zu Dashou's household, followed the campaigns with merit, and rose step by step to vice commander at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 部卒多塞外降人，所向克捷。

translations.literal: His troops were mostly surrenderers from beyond the passes; wherever they went they won.
translations.idiomatic: His men were mostly surrendered tribesmen from beyond the passes, and they seldom met defeat.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年七月，叛將李九成等圍萊州急，詔發關外兵討之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Chongzhen the rebel generals Li Jiucheng and others pressed Laizhou urgently; an edict dispatched troops from beyond the passes to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chongzhen year five the rebel Li Jiucheng and others pressed Laizhou hard; the court sent troops from beyond the passes against them.

sentences.zh: 寬與靳國臣、祖大弼、張韜率兵抵昌邑。

translations.literal: Kuan with Jin Guochen, Zu Dabi, and Zhang Tao led troops to Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan marched with Jin Guochen, Zu Dabi, and Zhang Tao to Changyi.

sentences.zh: 巡撫硃大黃典獲賊書，約寬等為內應，以示寬等。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Zhu Dahuang through an informer obtained rebel letters arranging Kuan and the others as inside responders, and showed them to Kuan's party.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Zhu Dahuang seized rebel letters through an informer that named Kuan's party as inside collaborators, and confronted them with the evidence.

sentences.zh: 皆誓滅賊以自明，乃用寬、國臣為前鋒。

translations.literal: All swore to destroy the bandits to clear themselves, and then Kuan and Guochen were made vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: They all swore to exterminate the rebels to prove their loyalty, and Kuan and Guochen were placed in the van.

sentences.zh: 寬至沙河與賊遇，眾寡不敵，稍卻。

translations.literal: Kuan at Shahe met the bandits; numbers were unequal and he gave ground slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan met the rebels at Shahe; outnumbered, he gave a little ground.

sentences.zh: 會國臣至，拔刀大呼直前，寬、大弼、韜鹹殊死戰，大敗賊兵，逐北抵城下，立解萊州圍。

translations.literal: When Guochen arrived he drew his saber and shouted, charging straight ahead; Kuan, Dabi, and Tao all fought to the death; they routed the bandit army, pursued north to below the walls, and the siege of Laizhou was lifted at once.
translations.idiomatic: Guochen came up, drew his blade, and charged with a roar; Kuan, Dabi, and Tao threw themselves into the fight; the rebel host broke, was chased to the walls, and the siege of Laizhou was lifted on the spot.

sentences.zh: 是月晦，進兵黃縣。

translations.literal: On the last day of that month they advanced to Huang County.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of that month they pushed on to Huang County.

sentences.zh: 賊傾巢出戰，寬等復大敗之，遂與劉澤清等築長圍以困登州。

translations.literal: The bandits came out in full force; Kuan and the others again routed them, then with Liu Zeqing and others built a long encirclement to hem in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came out in full strength; Kuan beat them again, then with Liu Zeqing and others threw a long cordon around Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，賊始平。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year the bandits were at last pacified.
translations.idiomatic: By the second month of the following year the rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 語詳《大典傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in the Biography of Da Dian.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign is told at length in the Biography of Zhu Dadian.

sentences.zh: 寬以解圍功，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: For merit in relieving the siege Kuan was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For lifting the siege Kuan was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 再敘功，世廕外衛副千戶，進副總兵。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded again: hereditary enfeoffment as vice battalion chief of an outer guard, and promotion to vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Further merit brought hereditary rank as vice battalion chief of an outer guard and promotion to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，命為援剿總兵官，督關外兵三千討流賊。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year he was appointed suppressing-and-pacifying regional commander, supervising three thousand troops from beyond the passes against the roaming bandits.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn of the eighth year he was named pacification commander, leading three thousand border troops against the roving rebels.

sentences.zh: 十月至河南，巡撫陳必謙、監紀推官湯開遠令與左良玉抵靈寶，至則挫張獻忠於焦村。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached Henan; Governor Chen Biqian and supervising secretary Tang Kaiyuan ordered him with Zuo Liangyu to reach Lingbao, and on arrival they repulsed Zhang Xianzhong at Jiaocun.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he entered Henan; Governor Chen Biqian and supervising secretary Tang Kaiyuan sent him with Zuo Liangyu to Lingbao, where they beat Zhang Xianzhong at Jiaocun.

sentences.zh: 無何，高迎祥、李自成至，與獻忠合攻閿鄉。

translations.literal: Before long Gao Yingxiang and Li Zicheng arrived, joined with Xianzhong, and together attacked Yingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Yingxiang and Li Zicheng came up, united with Xianzhong, and together struck Yingxiang.

sentences.zh: 寬赴救，賊解而趨靈寶，斷良玉、寬軍不相應，遂東陷陝州，攻洛陽。

translations.literal: Kuan went to relieve; the bandits disengaged and rushed toward Lingbao, cut off Liangyu's and Kuan's forces from mutual support, then east took Shanzhou and attacked Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan marched to relieve them; the rebels slipped away toward Lingbao, severed Liangyu and Kuan from each other, then swept east, took Shanzhou, and threatened Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 良玉、寬至，迎祥、自成、獻忠皆走。

translations.literal: When Liangyu and Kuan arrived, Yingxiang, Zicheng, and Xianzhong all fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangyu and Kuan came up, Yingxiang, Zicheng, and Xianzhong all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 良玉追迎祥，而寬分擊獻忠，夜督副將祖克勇等趨葛家莊，黎明遇賊，大破之。

translations.literal: Liangyu pursued Yingxiang while Kuan separately struck Xianzhong; by night he drove deputy commanders Zu Keyong and others to Gejiazhuang, met the bandits at dawn, and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu chased Yingxiang while Kuan turned on Xianzhong; he drove his deputies Zu Keyong and others through the night to Gejiazhuang and at dawn shattered the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 賊奔嵩縣九皋山，寬伏二軍於山溝誘之。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Jiugaoshan in Song County; Kuan ambushed two armies in the ravines to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Jiugao Mountain in Song; Kuan hid two bodies in the gullies to bait them down.

sentences.zh: 賊趨下，伏發，斬馘九百有奇。

translations.literal: The bandits rushed downhill; the ambush sprang and they cut off more than nine hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: As they rushed downhill the trap closed; more than nine hundred heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 尋與副將劉肇基、羅岱遇賊汝州圪料鎮，復大敗賊，伏屍二十餘里，斬馘千六百有奇。

translations.literal: Soon with deputy commanders Liu Zhaoqi and Luo Dai they met bandits at Gelia Town in Ruzhou, again routed them greatly—corpses lay twenty-odd li, more than sixteen hundred heads cut.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and deputies Liu Zhaoqi and Luo Dai met the rebels at Gelia in Ruzhou and broke them again—corpses stretched twenty li, with more than sixteen hundred heads counted.

sentences.zh: 獻忠憤，合迎祥、自成兵，與寬戰龍門、白沙，截官軍為二。

translations.literal: Xianzhong in fury united the armies of Yingxiang and Zicheng and fought Kuan at Longmen and Baisha, cutting the government army in two.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Xianzhong joined Yingxiang and Zicheng and met Kuan at Longmen and Baisha, slicing the government force in two.

sentences.zh: 寬自斷後，士卒殊死鬥，自晨至夜分，復大捷，斬馘一千有奇。

translations.literal: Kuan himself covered the rear; troops fought to the death from morning until deep into the night; again a great victory, more than a thousand heads cut.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan himself held the rear; his men fought to the death from dawn far into the night and won again, taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 迎祥、自成乃走窺光州，寬督副將李輔明躡其後。

translations.literal: Yingxiang and Zicheng then went to spy on Guangzhou; Kuan directed deputy commander Li Fuming to follow on their heels.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang and Zicheng then turned toward Guang prefecture; Kuan sent deputy Li Fuming to dog their steps.

sentences.zh: 賊走攻確山，寬等馳救，大破之，斬馘五百八十有奇。

translations.literal: The bandits turned to attack Queshan; Kuan and others raced to relieve, routed them greatly, more than five hundred eighty heads cut.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swung to attack Queshan; Kuan raced to its relief and crushed them, taking more than five hundred eighty heads.

sentences.zh: 自成等遂東走廬州，攻圍七晝夜。

translations.literal: Zicheng and the rest then fled east to Luzhou and besieged it seven days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng and the rest fled east to Luzhou and besieged it for seven days and nights.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，寬等至，賊奔全椒，遂圍滁州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Kuan and the others arrived; the bandits fled to Quanjiao and then besieged Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Kuan came up; the rebels fled to Quanjiao, then turned to besiege Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 南京太僕卿李覺斯、知州劉大鞏力禦之。

translations.literal: Nanjing Court of Imperial Stud Li Juesi and prefect Liu Dagong defended strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Juesi of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Stud and Prefect Liu Dagong held the city with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 而寬等軍至，奮擊大呼，諸軍無不一當百，自晨至晡，賊大敗。

translations.literal: When Kuan's army arrived they struck fiercely with loud shouts; every soldier fought as ten; from morning until afternoon the bandits were routed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuan arrived his men charged with a roar; each soldier fought like ten; from morning until afternoon the rebel host was shattered.

sentences.zh: 從城東五里追至關山之硃龍橋，橫屍枕藉，水為不流。

translations.literal: From five li east of the city they pursued to the Vermilion Dragon Bridge at Guanshan; bodies lay piled across the path and the water would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: They chased them five li east of the city to the Vermilion Dragon Bridge at Guanshan; the dead lay heaped and the water dammed with corpses.

sentences.zh: 二月，又從總理盧象升破賊七頂山，殲自成精卒殆盡。

translations.literal: In the second month again with Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng they broke the bandits at Seven-Peak Mountain and annihilated almost all of Zicheng's elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, with Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng, he broke the rebels at Seven-Peak Mountain and all but wiped out Zicheng's picked troops.

sentences.zh: 象升移軍南陽，命寬備鄧州。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng shifted army south to Nanyang and ordered Kuan to guard Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng moved south to Nanyang and left Kuan to hold Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 會賊渡漢江，入鄖、襄，余眾三萬匿內鄉、淅川山中。

translations.literal: The bandits crossed the Han River into Yun and Xiang; remaining troops of thirty thousand hid in the mountains of Neixiang and Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed the Han into Yun and Xiang; thirty thousand survivors hid in the mountains of Neixiang and Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 象升命寬與祖大樂等入山搜討。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng ordered Kuan with Zu Dale and others to enter the mountains and search them out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng ordered Kuan, Zu Dale, and others into the hills to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 邊軍強憨，性異他卒，不可以法繩。

translations.literal: Border troops were tough and obstinate, their nature unlike other soldiers', and could not be restrained by law.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops were hard and headstrong, unlike other soldiers, and would not bend to discipline.

sentences.zh: 往時官軍多關中人，與賊鄉里，臨陣相勞苦，拋生口，棄輜重，即縱之去，謂之「打活仗」。

translations.literal: Formerly government troops were mostly men from Guanzhong, fellow townsmen of the bandits; in battle they exchanged greetings, threw away captives, abandoned baggage, and let them go at once—this was called "fighting a live battle."
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days government troops were mostly Guanzhong men, often kin to the rebels; in battle they would hail one another, drop prisoners and baggage, and let the enemy slip away—a practice called "fighting a live battle."

sentences.zh: 邊軍不通言語，逢賊即殺，故多勝。

translations.literal: Border troops did not share a language; meeting bandits they killed at once, and so won more often.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops shared no tongue with the enemy; they killed on sight, and so won more often.

sentences.zh: 然所過焚廬舍，淫婦女，恃功不戢；

translations.literal: Yet wherever they passed they burned houses and ravished women, relying on merit unchastened;
translations.idiomatic: Yet they burned dwellings and violated women wherever they marched, swaggering on their victories;

sentences.zh: 又利野戰，憚搜山；

translations.literal: they also preferred open battle and dreaded searching mountains;
translations.idiomatic: they preferred open field fights and shrank from mountain sweeps;

sentences.zh: 且見賊遠竄，非旬朔可定，自以為客將，無持久心。

translations.literal: and seeing the bandits flee far, not decisive in a month or a fortnight, they took themselves as guest commanders without long-term heart.
translations.idiomatic: and seeing the rebels driven far off, with no end in a month or two, they counted themselves guest generals with no will to stay.

sentences.zh: 寬卒方過河，噪而逸。

translations.literal: Kuan's troops had just crossed the river when they clamored and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's men had barely crossed the river when they broke into mutinous clamor and bolted.

sentences.zh: 象升激勸再三，始聽命。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng exhorted them repeatedly; at last they obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng exhorted them again and again before they would listen.

sentences.zh: 至黨子口，仍按甲不行。

translations.literal: At Dangzikou they again held their armor and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Dangzi Pass they halted again and refused to march.

sentences.zh: 而總兵李重鎮素恇怯，冀卸責，眾益思歸。

translations.literal: Meanwhile regional commander Li Chongzhen was by nature timid and craven, hoping to shed responsibility, and the troops all the more wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Li Chongzhen was himself timid and hoped to escape blame; the men only wanted to go home.

sentences.zh: 象升乃力陳入山搜剿之難，請令寬、重鎮赴關中討賊。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng then set forth with force the difficulty of mountain search-and-suppression and requested that Kuan and Chongzhen be ordered to Guanzhong to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng then argued at length how hard mountain suppression was and asked that Kuan and Chongzhen be sent to Guanzhong to fight rebels there.

sentences.zh: 會總督洪承疇亦請之，寬等遂移軍陝西，隸承疇麾下。

translations.literal: Just then Governor-General Hong Chengchou also requested it, and Kuan and the others then moved army to Shaanxi under Chengchou's command.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Hong Chengchou asked the same; Kuan and his force were shifted to Shaanxi and placed under Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 八月，京師被兵，召入衛。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the capital came under attack; he was summoned to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, when the capital was besieged, he was called in to defend it.

sentences.zh: 錄滁州功，進右都督，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Recording his merit at Chuzhou, he was promoted to Right Commissioner-in-chief and bestowed silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: For his victory at Chuzhou he was promoted to Right Commissioner-in-chief and rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 事定，命赴寧遠協守。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was ordered to go to Ningyuan to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: After the crisis passed, he was ordered to Ningyuan to help hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，詔寬率師援畿輔。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year an edict ordered Kuan to lead his army to relieve the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year he was ordered to march to the capital region with his army.

sentences.zh: 及山東告急，寬逗遛。

translations.literal: When Shandong reported emergency, Kuan lingered and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong sent urgent appeals for help, Kuan dawdled on the road.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，濟南失守，褫職被逮，坐失陷籓封，竟棄市。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Jinan fell; his office was stripped and he was arrested, convicted of losing a princely fief, and in the end executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, Jinan fell; he was stripped of rank, arrested, convicted of allowing a princely domain to be lost, and finally executed in public.

sentences.zh: 寬敢戰有功，稱驍將。

translations.literal: Kuan dared to fight and had achievements, and was called a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was bold in battle and won real merit, and was accounted a fierce commander.

sentences.zh: 性剛使氣，不為文吏所喜，卒致大辟，莫為論救。

translations.literal: His nature was stubborn and he vented his temper; civil officials did not favor him, and in the end he suffered the great penalty, with no one pleading to save him.
translations.idiomatic: He was proud and quick to take offense, disliked by the civil bureaucracy; in the end he went to the block, and no one spoke up for him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：左良玉以驍勇之材，頻殲劇寇，遂擁強兵，驕亢自恣，緩則養寇以貽憂，急則棄甲以致潰。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Zuo Liangyu, with fierce and brave talent, repeatedly destroyed fierce bandits, and thus came to hold a strong army, proud and overbearing and self-indulgent—when slow he nourished bandits to bequeath worry, when urgent he cast off armor and caused rout.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Zuo Liangyu was a fierce fighter who repeatedly smashed major rebel bands and thereby came to command a huge army; arrogant and self-willed, in quiet times he let the rebels grow stronger and in crises he threw away his armor and brought on rout.

sentences.zh: 當時以不用命罪諸將者屢矣，而良玉偃蹇僨事，未正刑章，姑息釀患，是以卒至稱兵犯闕而不顧也。

translations.literal: At that time generals were repeatedly punished for disobeying orders, yet Liangyu was recalcitrant and ruined affairs without being brought to proper punishment—indulgence bred calamity, and thus in the end he raised troops and violated the imperial precinct without regard.
translations.idiomatic: In those days commanders were often punished for disobedience, yet Liangyu defied his superiors and wrecked campaigns without ever facing the law; indulgence bred disaster, until at last he marched on the court itself without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 高傑、祖寬皆剛悍難馴，恃功不戢，而傑尤為凶驁。

translations.literal: Gao Jie and Zu Kuan were both stubborn, fierce, and hard to tame, relying on merit and not restraining themselves—and Jie was especially savage and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie and Zu Kuan were both brutal and ungovernable, swollen with their victories and unwilling to submit—and Jie was the most violent and overbearing of all.

sentences.zh: 然傑被戕于銳意進取之時，寬受誅於力戰赴援之後，死非其罪，不能無遺憾焉。

translations.literal: Yet Jie was killed when keenly pressing forward in attack, and Kuan was executed after fighting hard to go to relief—their deaths were not their due crimes, and one cannot be without lingering regret.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jie was murdered at the height of an aggressive campaign, and Kuan was put to death after fighting his way to a relief mission; neither death matched his true deserts, and that leaves a bitter aftertaste.
